questions.question_text:
Fill the blank to say "I understand English."
```text
えいご ____ わかります。
(eigo ____ wakarimasu.)
```

options.A: に (ni)
options.B: と (to)
options.C: の (no)
options.D: が (ga)

questions.explanation: わかります (wakarimasu) (to understand) takes the thing understood with が (ga): えいごが わかります (eigo ga wakarimasu).

questions.question_text: When do you say ただいま (tadaima)?

options.A: When you leave home
options.B: When you start eating
options.C: When you apologize
options.D: When you arrive back home ("I'm back")

questions.explanation: ただいま (tadaima) is said on returning home, and the person at home answers おかえりなさい (okaeri nasai) ("welcome back"). When leaving home you say いってきます (ittekimasu) and are answered with いってらっしゃい (itterasshai).

questions.question_text:
Fill the blank to say "a car of Japan" (a Japanese car).
```text
にほん ____ くるま
(nihon ____ kuruma)
```

options.A: の (no)
options.B: は (wa)
options.C: を (o)
options.D: か (ka)

questions.explanation: の (no) links two nouns like "of", with the owner or origin first: にほんの くるま (nihon no kuruma). Another example: ブラジルの コーヒー (burajiru no kōhī) (coffee of Brazil).

questions.question_text:
Fill the blank to introduce yourself: "I am Ken."
```text
はじめまして。わたし ____ ケンです。
(hajimemashite. watashi ____ ken desu.)
```

options.A: は (wa)
options.B: を (o)
options.C: か (ka)
options.D: と (to)

questions.explanation: The topic particle は (wa) (written は, read "wa") follows わたし (watashi) to give わたしは ケンです (watashi wa ken desu), "I am Ken."

questions.question_text: Which sentence is the correct question form of それは パンです (sore wa pan desu) ("That is bread")?

options.A: か それは パンです (ka sore wa pan desu)
options.B: それは パンですか (sore wa pan desu ka)
options.C: それは か パンです (sore wa ka pan desu)
options.D: それは パンですを (sore wa pan desu o)

questions.explanation: This is the question particle か (ka): put it at the very end of a statement to turn it into a question, with no change in word order. Another example: これは コーヒーですか (kore wa kōhī desu ka) ("Is this coffee?").

questions.question_text: Possession formula: $\text{owner} + no + \text{thing}$. How do you say "the teacher's book" (teacher = せんせい (sensei), book = ほん (hon))?

options.A: ほんの せんせい (hon no sensei)
options.B: せんせいと ほん (sensei to hon)
options.C: せんせいの ほん (sensei no hon)
options.D: せんせいを ほん (sensei o hon)

questions.explanation: The owner comes first and の (no) follows it, the reverse of English word order in "book of the teacher". ほんの せんせい (hon no sensei) would mean "the book's teacher".

questions.question_text: Which sentence is correct for "I will go tomorrow"?

options.A: あしたに いきます (ashita ni ikimasu)
options.B: あしたを いきます (ashita o ikimasu)
options.C: あしたの いきます (ashita no ikimasu)
options.D: あした いきます (ashita ikimasu)

questions.explanation: Relative time words such as あした (ashita) (tomorrow), きょう (kyō) (today) and まいにち (mainichi) (every day) take no particle に (ni), while a clock time does: くじに いきます (kuji ni ikimasu) (I go at nine).

questions.question_text: What does ごご (gogo) mean when telling the time?

options.A: a.m. (morning)
options.B: exactly on the hour
options.C: half past
options.D: p.m. (afternoon or evening)

questions.explanation: ごご (gogo) means p.m. and ごぜん (gozen) means a.m., as in ごご さんじ (gogo sanji) (3 p.m.). "Exactly on the hour" is ちょうど (chōdo) and "half past" is はん (han).

questions.question_text: Which word means "the language spoken in Brazil"?

options.A: ブラジルご (burajirugo)
options.B: ブラジルじん (burajirujin)
options.C: ポルトガルご (porutogarugo)
options.D: スペインご (supeingo)

questions.explanation: People in Brazil speak Portuguese, so the language is ポルトガルご (porutogarugo). ブラジルじん (burajirujin) means a Brazilian person, and スペインご (supeingo) is Spanish.

questions.question_text: When do you say こんばんは (konbanwa)?

options.A: When going to bed
options.B: When greeting someone in the evening
options.C: When arriving home
options.D: When meeting someone for the first time

questions.explanation: こんばんは (konbanwa) means "good evening" and is said when you meet someone at night. Going to bed uses おやすみなさい (oyasumi nasai), arriving home uses ただいま (tadaima), and a first meeting uses はじめまして (hajimemashite).

questions.question_text: Time-point formula: $\text{time} + ni + \text{verb}$. Which sentence means "I wake up at six" (6 o'clock = ろくじ (rokuji), wake up = おきます (okimasu))?

options.A: ろくじを おきます (rokuji o okimasu)
options.B: ろくじが おきます (rokuji ga okimasu)
options.C: ろくじに おきます (rokuji ni okimasu)
options.D: ろくじで おきます (rokuji de okimasu)

questions.explanation: The particle に (ni) marks an exact point in time, so ろくじに (rokuji ni) means "at six". Another example: じゅうじに ねます (jūji ni nemasu) (I sleep at ten).

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.
```text
コーヒーを ふたつ ください。
(kōhī o futatsu kudasai.)
Translation: ____
```

options.A: Coffee and tea, please.
options.B: Two coffees, please.
options.C: Two teas, please.
options.D: I drank two coffees.

questions.explanation: コーヒー (kōhī) is coffee, ふたつ (futatsu) is "two" and ください (kudasai) is "please give me". The pattern is thing + を (o) + quantity + ください (kudasai).

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.
```text
すみません、くうこうは どこですか。
(sumimasen, kūkō wa doko desu ka.)
Translation: ____
```

options.A: Excuse me, where is the airport?
options.B: Excuse me, is this the airport?
options.C: Excuse me, the airport is over there.
options.D: Excuse me, where is the subway?

questions.explanation: すみません (sumimasen) gets attention, くうこう (kūkō) is the airport, どこ (doko) is "where" and か (ka) turns the sentence into a question.

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.
```text
いま、ごじはんです。
(ima, goji han desu.)
Translation: ____
```

options.A: It is 5:00 now.
options.B: It is 5:30 now.
options.C: It is 5:45 now.
options.D: It is 6:30 now.

questions.explanation: ごじ (goji) is 5 o'clock and はん (han) adds "half past", so ごじはん (goji han) is 5:30. いま (ima) means "now".

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says "I speak English"?

options.A: えいごが はなします (eigo ga hanashimasu)
options.B: えいごに はなします (eigo ni hanashimasu)
options.C: えいごの はなします (eigo no hanashimasu)
options.D: えいごを はなします (eigo o hanashimasu)

questions.explanation: はなします (hanashimasu) (to speak) takes the object particle を (o), while わかります (wakarimasu) (to understand) takes が (ga). Another example: にほんごを べんきょうします (nihongo o benkyō shimasu) (I study Japanese).

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.
```text
しごとは くじから ごじまでです。
(shigoto wa kuji kara goji made desu.)
Translation: ____
```

options.A: Work is from 9 to 5.
options.B: Work starts at 5 and ends at 9.
options.C: Work is at 9 and at 5.
options.D: Work lasts nine hours.

questions.explanation: から (kara) marks the start and まで (made) the end: くじから ごじまで (kuji kara goji made) is "from 9 until 5". しごと (shigoto) means work.

questions.question_text: Which word means "the English language"?

options.A: イギリスご (igirisugo)
options.B: えいご (eigo)
options.C: アメリカご (amerikago)
options.D: にほんご (nihongo)

questions.explanation: English has its own word, えいご (eigo); it is an exception to the "country + ご" pattern. にほんご (nihongo) means Japanese, while イギリスご (igirisugo) and アメリカご (amerikago) are not used.

questions.question_text: Choose the particle that marks origin: ブラジル ____ きました (burajiru ____ kimashita) ("I came from Brazil").

options.A: まで (made)
options.B: に (ni)
options.C: と (to)
options.D: から (kara)

questions.explanation: The particle から (kara) means "from" and marks a starting point or origin. Another example: サンパウロから きました (sanpauro kara kimashita) (I came from São Paulo). まで (made) means "until" and に (ni) would mean "came to".

questions.question_text: The very formal way to give your name follows the formula $\text{name} + to + mōshimasu$. How do you say "My name is Maria" (マリア (maria)) this way?

options.A: マリアと もうします (maria to mōshimasu)
options.B: マリアを もうします (maria o mōshimasu)
options.C: マリアさんと もうします (maria-san to mōshimasu)
options.D: マリアと です (maria to desu)

questions.explanation: The particle と (to) followed by もうします (mōshimasu) is a very formal "I am called ...". As always, さん (san) is not added to your own name. The everyday version is わたしは マリアです (watashi wa maria desu).

questions.question_text: In katakana words such as コーヒー (kōhī), what does the long mark ー (chōonpu) do?

options.A: It makes the word a question
options.B: It lengthens the vowel before it
options.C: It silences the vowel before it
options.D: It shows the word is plural

questions.explanation: The long-vowel mark ー stretches the previous vowel, so コーヒー (kōhī) is "kōhī" with a long ō and a long ī, not "kohi". Another example: ケーキ (kēki) has a long ē.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly introduces yourself ("I am Maria")?

options.A: わたしは マリアです (watashi wa maria desu)
options.B: わたしは マリアさんです (watashi wa maria-san desu)
options.C: わたしを マリアです (watashi o maria desu)
options.D: わたしと マリアです (watashi to maria desu)

questions.explanation: The honorific suffix さん (san) is for talking about other people, never about yourself. Use topic は (wa) + name + です (desu). For someone else: たなかさんは せんせいです (tanaka-san wa sensei desu).

questions.question_text:
Fill the blank to say "Good morning" politely.
```text
____ ございます。
(____ gozaimasu.)
```

options.A: こんにちは (konnichiwa)
options.B: さようなら (sayōnara)
options.C: ただいま (tadaima)
options.D: おはよう (ohayō)

questions.explanation: Adding ございます (gozaimasu) to おはよう (ohayō) gives the polite morning greeting おはようございます (ohayō gozaimasu). こんにちは (konnichiwa) is a daytime greeting, さようなら (sayōnara) is goodbye and ただいま (tadaima) is "I'm home".

questions.question_text: When you order food or a drink in Japanese, what does ください (kudasai) express?

options.A: Thanks: "thank you very much"
options.B: A compliment: "it is delicious"
options.C: A polite request: "please give me ..."
options.D: An attention-getter: "excuse me"

questions.explanation: ください (kudasai) follows the thing you want and means "please give me". For example みずを ください (mizu o kudasai) is "Water, please." Thanks is ありがとうございます (arigatō gozaimasu), delicious is おいしい (oishii), and "excuse me" is すみません (sumimasen).

questions.question_text: Use $\text{thing} + o + \text{quantity} + kudasai$ to say "Three cakes, please" (cake = ケーキ (kēki), three = みっつ (mittsu)).

options.A: ケーキを ふたつ ください (kēki o futatsu kudasai)
options.B: ケーキを よっつ ください (kēki o yottsu kudasai)
options.C: ケーキを いつつ ください (kēki o itsutsu kudasai)
options.D: ケーキを みっつ ください (kēki o mittsu kudasai)

questions.explanation: The generic counter gives ひとつ (hitotsu) (1), ふたつ (futatsu) (2), みっつ (mittsu) (3), よっつ (yottsu) (4) and いつつ (itsutsu) (5). The noun ケーキ (kēki) stays unchanged; only the number shows the quantity.

questions.question_text: Time formula: $\text{hour} + ji + han$ means "half past". How do you say 7:30 (7 o'clock = しちじ (shichiji))?

options.A: ななじはん (nanaji han)
options.B: しちじぷん (shichiji pun)
options.C: しちじはん (shichiji han)
options.D: しちじ ちょうど (shichiji chōdo)

questions.explanation: Seven o'clock is irregular, しちじ (shichiji), and はん (han) adds the half hour. ちょうど (chōdo) means "exactly" (7:00 sharp), and ななじ (nanaji) is not used.

questions.question_text: Sentence formula: $\text{person} + san + no + \text{thing} + wa + \text{place} + desu$. Which sentence says "Mr. Tanaka's ticket is here" (ticket = きっぷ (kippu), here = ここ (koko))?

options.A: きっぷの たなかさんは ここです (kippu no tanaka-san wa koko desu)
options.B: たなかさんの ここは きっぷです (tanaka-san no koko wa kippu desu)
options.C: たなかさんを きっぷは ここです (tanaka-san o kippu wa koko desu)
options.D: たなかさんの きっぷは ここです (tanaka-san no kippu wa koko desu)

questions.explanation: たなかさんの きっぷ (tanaka-san no kippu) is "Mr. Tanaka's ticket" (owner + の (no) + thing), then the topic は (wa) and the location with です (desu).

questions.question_text: In がっこうへ いきます (gakkō e ikimasu) ("I go to school"), how is the particle written へ (e) read and what does it mark?

options.A: It is read "he" and marks the direction
options.B: It is read "e" and marks the direction of movement
options.C: It is read "wa" and marks the topic
options.D: It is read "o" and marks the object

questions.explanation: This is the direction particle へ (e), written he but pronounced "e". With movement verbs it marks the destination: うちへ かえります (uchi e kaerimasu) (I go back home). Like it, は (wa) is read "wa" and を (o) is read "o".

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.
```text
バスていは あそこです。
(basutei wa asoko desu.)
Translation: ____
```

options.A: The bus stop is over there.
options.B: The bus stop is here.
options.C: Where is the bus stop?
options.D: This is not a bus stop.

questions.explanation: あそこ (asoko) means "over there" (far from both speaker and listener). ここ (koko) is "here" and どこ (doko) is "where".

questions.question_text:
Fill the blank: "There is a cat inside the house."
```text
いえの なかに ねこが ____。
(ie no naka ni neko ga ____.)
```

options.A: あります (arimasu)
options.B: いません (imasen)
options.C: ありません (arimasen)
options.D: います (imasu)

questions.explanation: A cat is a living animal, so existence is expressed with います (imasu). あります (arimasu) is for objects, and the other two are negatives ("there is not").

questions.question_text:
Fill the blank to say "Bread and cake, please."
```text
パン ____ ケーキを ください。
(pan ____ kēki o kudasai.)
```

options.A: か (ka)
options.B: は (wa)
options.C: と (to)
options.D: に (ni)

questions.explanation: と (to) joins two nouns like "and", giving パンと ケーキ (pan to kēki) (bread and cake). か (ka) would make a question or mean "or", and は (wa) marks a topic.

questions.question_text: パンを ふたつ ください (pan o futatsu kudasai) means "Two breads, please." How does Japanese show that there are two?

options.A: パン (pan) takes a plural ending
options.B: The noun パン (pan) does not change; the number ふたつ (futatsu) shows the quantity
options.C: を (o) changes to a plural particle
options.D: ください (kudasai) changes form

questions.explanation: Japanese nouns have no articles and, for the most part, no plural forms: みず (mizu) can be "water", "the water" or "a water". Quantity is expressed by a number or counter, such as ケーキを みっつ (kēki o mittsu) (three cakes).

questions.question_text: To ask for something, use the formula $\text{thing} + o + kudasai$. Which sentence means "Water, please" ($\text{thing} = $ みず (mizu))?

options.A: みずを ください (mizu o kudasai)
options.B: みずが ください (mizu ga kudasai)
options.C: ください みずを (kudasai mizu o)
options.D: みずの ください (mizu no kudasai)

questions.explanation: Put the object particle を (o) after the thing and finish with the request ください (kudasai). The verb-like word always comes last, so ください みずを (kudasai mizu o) is wrong.

questions.question_text: Which writing system is normally used for foreign loanwords such as ケーキ (kēki) (cake) and ジュース (jūsu) (juice)?

options.A: Katakana
options.B: Hiragana
options.C: Kanji
options.D: Rōmaji only

questions.explanation: Katakana is the script for words borrowed from other languages. Native Japanese words such as みず (mizu) (water) and ごはん (gohan) (rice, meal) are written in hiragana or kanji.

questions.question_text: What is the standard reply to ありがとうございます (arigatō gozaimasu) ("thank you very much")?

options.A: どういたしまして (dō itashimashite) ("you're welcome")
options.B: ただいま (tadaima)
options.C: はじめまして (hajimemashite)
options.D: おやすみなさい (oyasumi nasai)

questions.explanation: どういたしまして (dō itashimashite) means "you're welcome". A casual reply among friends is いえいえ (ieie). The other choices are for coming home, a first meeting and going to bed.

questions.question_text: What does うしろ (ushiro) mean?

options.A: Behind
options.B: In front of
options.C: Inside
options.D: Next to

questions.explanation: うしろ (ushiro) means "behind". Its relatives: まえ (mae) (in front), なか (naka) (inside) and となり (tonari) (next to). It works as in いすの うしろ (isu no ushiro) (behind the chair).

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.
```text
かぎは つくえの うえに あります。
(kagi wa tsukue no ue ni arimasu.)
Translation: ____
```

options.A: The key is under the desk.
options.B: The key is on the desk.
options.C: The desk is next to the key.
options.D: The key is inside the bag.

questions.explanation: かぎ (kagi) is key, つくえ (tsukue) is desk and うえ (ue) is "top, above", so つくえの うえ (tsukue no ue) is "on the desk". あります (arimasu) says that a thing exists there.

questions.question_text: Which particle marks the place where something exists in へやに ベッドが あります (heya ni beddo ga arimasu) ("There is a bed in the room")?

options.A: で (de)
options.B: に (ni)
options.C: を (o)
options.D: と (to)

questions.explanation: This is the location particle に (ni) used with existence verbs あります (arimasu) and います (imasu). The particle で (de) marks where an action takes place instead. Another example: いえに ねこが います (ie ni neko ga imasu).

questions.question_text: In which situation do you say おやすみなさい (oyasumi nasai)?

options.A: To greet someone in the morning
options.B: To introduce yourself
options.C: To thank someone after a meal
options.D: To wish someone good night before sleep

questions.explanation: おやすみなさい (oyasumi nasai) is used only when someone is going to sleep; its short informal form is おやすみ (oyasumi). It is not a general goodbye: for that use またね (mata ne) or さようなら (sayōnara).

questions.question_text: Which is the correct order for "coffee of Brazil" (Brazilian coffee), using the possessive/linking particle の (no)?

options.A: コーヒーの ブラジル (kōhī no burajiru)
options.B: コーヒー ブラジルの (kōhī burajiru no)
options.C: ブラジルの コーヒー (burajiru no kōhī)
options.D: ブラジル コーヒーの (burajiru kōhī no)

questions.explanation: In the pattern A の (no) B, the modifier (owner, origin) comes first and the main noun last; this is the particle の (no) of possession and origin. Another example: わたしの ともだち (watashi no tomodachi) (my friend).

questions.question_text: Complete with the particle that means "also": わたし ____ みずを ください (watashi ____ mizu o kudasai) ("Water for me too, please").

options.A: の (no)
options.B: と (to)
options.C: も (mo)
options.D: か (ka)

questions.explanation: The particle も (mo) ("also") replaces は (wa) or を (o) when the idea is "too". Another example: わたしも げんきです (watashi mo genki desu) ("I am fine too").

questions.question_text: Language formula: $\text{country} + go$. What is "the German language" (country = ドイツ (doitsu))?

options.A: ドイツじん (doitsujin)
options.B: ドイツの (doitsu no)
options.C: ドイツご (doitsugo)
options.D: ドイツを (doitsu o)

questions.explanation: Adding ご (go) (language) gives ドイツご (doitsugo); similarly フランスご (furansugo) is French. ドイツじん (doitsujin) would be a German person.

questions.question_text: Which verb completes ともだちが ____ (tomodachi ga ____) ("I have friends" / "there are friends")?

options.A: あります (arimasu)
options.B: います (imasu)
options.C: ありません (arimasen)
options.D: いません (imasen)

questions.explanation: Existence of people and animals uses います (imasu); things use あります (arimasu). The negatives are いません (imasen) and ありません (arimasen). Another example: こうえんに こどもが います (kōen ni kodomo ga imasu) (there are children in the park).

questions.question_text: How do you say "4 o'clock" in Japanese?

options.A: よじ (yoji)
options.B: よんじ (yonji)
options.C: しじ (shiji)
options.D: ようじ (yōji)

questions.explanation: Four o'clock has a special reading, よじ (yoji). Similarly, 7 o'clock is しちじ (shichiji) and 9 o'clock is くじ (kuji). The other hours are regular, such as ごじ (goji) (5 o'clock).

questions.question_text: What does ちかてつ (chikatetsu) mean?

options.A: Airport
options.B: Umbrella
options.C: Subway
options.D: Ticket

questions.explanation: ちかてつ (chikatetsu) is the subway. The airport is くうこう (kūkō), an umbrella is かさ (kasa) and a ticket is きっぷ (kippu).

questions.question_text: In the phrase `パンと コーヒー (pan to kōhī)`, what does the particle `と (to)` do?

options.A: It marks the direct object
options.B: It turns the phrase into a question
options.C: It means "also"
options.D: It joins two nouns, like "and"

questions.explanation: This is the noun-linking particle と (to) ("and"): パンと コーヒー (pan to kōhī) is "bread and coffee". It joins nouns only, not whole sentences. Another example: ほんと ノート (hon to nōto) (a book and a notebook).

questions.question_text: Existence formula: $\text{place} + ni + \text{thing} + ga + arimasu$. Which sentence means "There is a computer on the desk" (パソコン (pasokon))?

options.A: つくえの うえで パソコンが あります (tsukue no ue de pasokon ga arimasu)
options.B: つくえの うえに パソコンが あります (tsukue no ue ni pasokon ga arimasu)
options.C: つくえの うえに パソコンが います (tsukue no ue ni pasokon ga imasu)
options.D: パソコンの うえに つくえが あります (pasokon no ue ni tsukue ga arimasu)

questions.explanation: The place takes に (ni), the thing takes が (ga), and an object uses あります (arimasu). The last option reverses the meaning ("there is a desk on the computer").

questions.question_text: In ちずは どこですか (chizu wa doko desu ka) ("Where is the map?"), what is the role of は (wa)?

options.A: It is read "ha" and marks the direct object
options.B: It is read "wa" and marks possession
options.C: It is read "wa" and marks the topic of the sentence
options.D: It is read "o" and marks the destination

questions.explanation: This is the topic particle は (wa): it names what the sentence is about (the map) before the comment. Another example: くうこうは あそこです (kūkō wa asoko desu) (as for the airport, it is over there).

questions.question_text: Nationality formula: $\text{country} + jin$. What is the word for "Canadian person" (country = カナダ (kanada))?

options.A: カナダご (kanadago)
options.B: カナダの (kanada no)
options.C: カナダじん (kanadajin)
options.D: カナダを (kanada o)

questions.explanation: Adding じん (jin) (person) to a country gives the nationality: カナダじん (kanadajin), ブラジルじん (burajirujin), フランスじん (furansujin). ご (go) would make a language word instead.

questions.question_text: Interval formula: $\text{start} + kara + \text{end} + made$. How do you say "from 10 until 3"?

options.A: じゅうじから さんじまで (jūji kara sanji made)
options.B: さんじから じゅうじまで (sanji kara jūji made)
options.C: じゅうじまで さんじから (jūji made sanji kara)
options.D: じゅうじに さんじまで (jūji ni sanji made)

questions.explanation: から (kara) follows the starting time and まで (made) follows the ending time. Swapping them reverses the meaning to "from 3 until 10".

questions.question_text: Use the formula $\text{greeting} + \text{surname} + san$ to say "Good evening, Mr. Satō" (さとう (satō)).

options.A: こんにちは、さとうさん (konnichiwa, satō-san)
options.B: こんばんは、さとうさん (konbanwa, satō-san)
options.C: おはよう、さとうさん (ohayō, satō-san)
options.D: こんばんは、さとうを (konbanwa, satō o)

questions.explanation: Evening is こんばんは (konbanwa), followed by the surname and さん (san). こんにちは (konnichiwa) is for the daytime and おはよう (ohayō) for the morning.

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.
```text
このけいたいは だれのですか。
(kono keitai wa dare no desu ka.)
Translation: ____
```

options.A: Whose cell phone is this?
options.B: Where is this cell phone?
options.C: Is this your cell phone?
options.D: What is this cell phone?

questions.explanation: だれの (dare no) means "whose" (a person + the possessive の (no)), and このけいたい (kono keitai) is "this cell phone". A typical answer is わたしのです (watashi no desu) ("it is mine").

questions.question_text: A colleague leaves the office first and says おさきに しつれいします (osaki ni shitsurei shimasu) ("excuse me for leaving ahead of you"). What is the typical reply?

options.A: ただいま (tadaima)
options.B: いただきます (itadakimasu)
options.C: ようこそ (yōkoso)
options.D: おつかれさまでした (otsukaresama deshita)

questions.explanation: おつかれさまでした (otsukaresama deshita) acknowledges the other person's work ("thanks for your effort") and is the standard workplace reply. ようこそ (yōkoso) is "welcome", ただいま (tadaima) is "I'm home" and いただきます (itadakimasu) is said before eating.

questions.question_text: The country name にほん (nihon) (Japan) has another accepted reading. Which one?

options.A: にほんご (nihongo)
options.B: にほんじん (nihonjin)
options.C: ちゅうごく (chūgoku)
options.D: にっぽん (nippon)

questions.explanation: Both にほん (nihon) and にっぽん (nippon) are correct readings of the country's name. にほんご (nihongo) is the language and にほんじん (nihonjin) a Japanese person, while ちゅうごく (chūgoku) is China.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says "I don't have a car"?

options.A: わたしは くるまが ありません (watashi wa kuruma ga arimasen)
options.B: わたしは くるまを ありません (watashi wa kuruma o arimasen)
options.C: わたしは くるまが いません (watashi wa kuruma ga imasen)
options.D: わたしは くるまの ありません (watashi wa kuruma no arimasen)

questions.explanation: Possession of objects is expressed with the existence verb あります (arimasu) (negative ありません (arimasen)) and が (ga) marks the thing possessed. A car is inanimate, so いません (imasen) is wrong. Another example: わたしは パソコンが あります (watashi wa pasokon ga arimasu) (I have a computer).

questions.question_text: What is the difference between さんじ (sanji) and さんじかん (sanjikan)?

options.A: さんじ (sanji) is 3 o'clock (a point in time); さんじかん (sanjikan) is three hours (a duration)
options.B: さんじ (sanji) is three hours; さんじかん (sanjikan) is 3 o'clock
options.C: They mean the same; かん (kan) is just polite
options.D: さんじ (sanji) is 3 a.m. and さんじかん (sanjikan) is 3 p.m.

questions.explanation: じ (ji) counts clock hours, while じかん (jikan) counts the length of time. Compare くじに おきます (kuji ni okimasu) (I get up at nine) with くじかん ねます (kujikan nemasu) (I sleep nine hours).

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says "The bag is under the chair"?

options.A: かばんは した いすに あります (kaban wa shita isu ni arimasu)
options.B: かばんは いすを したに あります (kaban wa isu o shita ni arimasu)
options.C: かばんは いすの したに あります (kaban wa isu no shita ni arimasu)
options.D: かばんは いすの したを あります (kaban wa isu no shita o arimasu)

questions.explanation: Position words are nouns, so the pattern is reference object + の (no) + position noun + に (ni) + あります (arimasu). Another example: ほんは かばんの なかに あります (hon wa kaban no naka ni arimasu) (the book is inside the bag).

questions.question_text: Which pair of fixed phrases is said before and after a meal, in that order?

options.A: いただきます (itadakimasu) before, ごちそうさまでした (gochisōsama deshita) after
options.B: ごちそうさまでした (gochisōsama deshita) before, いただきます (itadakimasu) after
options.C: いただきます (itadakimasu) before, おかえりなさい (okaeri nasai) after
options.D: おはよう (ohayō) before, おやすみ (oyasumi) after

questions.explanation: いただきます (itadakimasu) ("I gratefully receive") starts the meal and ごちそうさまでした (gochisōsama deshita) ("thank you for the feast") ends it. Fixed formulas like these are learned as whole phrases rather than translated word by word.

questions.question_text: Choose the particle: としょかん ____ べんきょうします (toshokan ____ benkyō shimasu) ("I study at the library"; としょかん (toshokan) = library).

options.A: に (ni)
options.B: で (de)
options.C: を (o)
options.D: が (ga)

questions.explanation: This is the particle で (de) for the place where an action happens. The particle に (ni) marks where something exists (へやに ベッドが あります (heya ni beddo ga arimasu)). Another action example: うちで ごはんを たべます (uchi de gohan o tabemasu) (I eat at home).

questions.question_text: Time formula: $\text{hour} + ji + \text{minutes} + fun/pun$. How do you say 3:20?

options.A: さんじ にじゅうふん (sanji nijūfun)
options.B: さんじ にじゅうぷん (sanji nijūpun)
options.C: さんじ ふたじゅっぷん (sanji futajuppun)
options.D: さんじ にじゅっぷん (sanji nijuppun)

questions.explanation: Twenty minutes is にじゅっぷん (nijuppun): the tens word ends in a doubled consonant before the counter. Hours stay regular here, so 3 o'clock is さんじ (sanji). Another example: 6:10 is ろくじ じゅっぷん (rokuji juppun).

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.
```text
すみません、メニューを ください。
(sumimasen, menyū o kudasai.)
Translation: ____
```

options.A: Excuse me, what is the menu?
options.B: Excuse me, the menu is here.
options.C: Thank you, I read the menu.
options.D: Excuse me, the menu, please.

questions.explanation: すみません (sumimasen) gets the waiter's attention, メニュー (menyū) is the object marked by を (o), and ください (kudasai) makes the request.

questions.question_text:
Fill in the blank to answer "No, it is not mine."
```text
A: これは あなたの かさですか。 (kore wa anata no kasa desu ka.)
B: いいえ、わたしの ____ ありません。 (iie, watashi no ____ arimasen.)
```

options.A: は (wa)
options.B: じゃ (ja)
options.C: を (o)
options.D: に (ni)

questions.explanation: The polite negative of です (desu) is じゃ ありません (ja arimasen) (or では ありません (dewa arimasen)). The noun after わたしの (watashi no) is dropped because it is clear from context.

questions.question_text: Question formula: $\text{owner} + san + no + \text{thing} + wa + doko + desu + ka$. Which sentence means "Where is Mr. Tanaka's umbrella?"

options.A: かさの たなかさんは どこですか (kasa no tanaka-san wa doko desu ka)
options.B: たなかさんの かさは どこですか (tanaka-san no kasa wa doko desu ka)
options.C: たなかさんは かさの どこですか (tanaka-san wa kasa no doko desu ka)
options.D: たなかさんの どこは かさですか (tanaka-san no doko wa kasa desu ka)

questions.explanation: Owner + の (no) + thing forms the topic, どこ (doko) asks for the place, and か (ka) closes the question. Another example: わたしの ぼうしは どこですか (watashi no bōshi wa doko desu ka).

questions.question_text:
Complete the dialogue so that B says "I am fine too."
```text
A: おげんきですか。 (ogenki desu ka.)
B: はい、げんきです。あなたは？ (hai, genki desu. anata wa?)
A: わたし ____ げんきです。 (watashi ____ genki desu.)
```

options.A: を (o)
options.B: が (ga)
options.C: も (mo)
options.D: の (no)

questions.explanation: も (mo) takes the place of は (wa) to say "also": わたしも げんきです (watashi mo genki desu). The question あなたは？ (anata wa?) ("and you?") hands the same question back lightly.

questions.question_text: The sentence `それは わたしの かばんです (sore wa watashi no kaban desu)` can be shortened by dropping the repeated noun. Which is the correct short form?

options.A: それは わたしのかばんのです (sore wa watashi no kaban no desu)
options.B: それは わたしのです (sore wa watashi no desu)
options.C: それは わたしです (sore wa watashi desu)
options.D: それは わたしを です (sore wa watashi o desu)

questions.explanation: Here の (no) works as a noun substitute ("the one of mine") when the thing is clear from context. This is the pronoun-like use of の (no). Another example: この かさは ともだちのです (kono kasa wa tomodachi no desu) (this umbrella is my friend's).

questions.question_text: Which statement about the polite verb おきます (okimasu) ("wake up") is correct?

options.A: It takes a different ending when the subject is a third person
options.B: The same form is used for I, you and he/she; ます (masu) does not change with the person
options.C: It gets a plural ending when several people wake up
options.D: It changes ending depending on the gender of the speaker

questions.explanation: This is the polite ます (masu) form: it conjugates for tense and polarity (おきました (okimashita) past, おきません (okimasen) negative), but never for person, number or gender. Another example: わたしは ねます (watashi wa nemasu) and かれは ねます (kare wa nemasu) both use ねます (nemasu).

questions.question_text: Which pair correctly gives "a Brazilian person" and "the language of Brazil"?

options.A: ブラジルじん (burajirujin) and ポルトガルご (porutogarugo)
options.B: ブラジルじん (burajirujin) and ブラジルご (burajirugo)
options.C: ポルトガルじん (porutogarujin) and ポルトガルご (porutogarugo)
options.D: ブラジルご (burajirugo) and ブラジルじん (burajirujin)

questions.explanation: The nationality is country + じん (jin), but the language is named after Portuguese: ポルトガルご (porutogarugo). ポルトガルじん (porutogarujin) is a person from Portugal, and "ブラジルご (burajirugo)" is not used.

questions.question_text: For afternoon times, the 24-hour clock follows $h_{24} = h_{12} + 12$. How is 8 p.m. said on a 24-hour clock?

options.A: にじゅうじ (nijūji)
options.B: じゅうはちじ (jūhachiji)
options.C: にじゅういちじ (nijūichiji)
options.D: はちじ (hachiji)

questions.explanation: 8 + 12 = 20, so 8 p.m. is にじゅうじ (nijūji) (20:00). じゅうはちじ (jūhachiji) is 18:00 (6 p.m.) and にじゅういちじ (nijūichiji) is 21:00. Likewise 3 p.m. is じゅうごじ (jūgoji).

questions.question_text: Politeness formula: $\text{casual form} + gozaimasu$ (as in おはよう (ohayō) > おはようございます (ohayō gozaimasu)). Applying it, what is the polite form of ありがとう (arigatō) ("thanks")?

options.A: ありがとうなさい (arigatō nasai)
options.B: ありがとうございます (arigatō gozaimasu)
options.C: ありがとうます (arigatō masu)
options.D: ありがとうでした (arigatō deshita)

questions.explanation: ございます (gozaimasu) raises both おはよう (ohayō) and ありがとう (arigatō) to the polite level. なさい (nasai) is used for other pairs, such as おやすみ (oyasumi) > おやすみなさい (oyasumi nasai) and ごめん (gomen) > ごめんなさい (gomen nasai).

questions.question_text: Formula for people: $\text{person} + wa + \text{place} + ni + imasu$. Which sentence means "My friend is in the park" (こうえん (kōen))?

options.A: わたしの ともだちは こうえんに います (watashi no tomodachi wa kōen ni imasu)
options.B: わたしの ともだちは こうえんに あります (watashi no tomodachi wa kōen ni arimasu)
options.C: わたしの ともだちは こうえんで います (watashi no tomodachi wa kōen de imasu)
options.D: わたしの ともだちは こうえんを います (watashi no tomodachi wa kōen o imasu)

questions.explanation: A person uses います (imasu) and the place of existence takes に (ni). あります (arimasu) is for inanimate things and で (de) marks the place of an action.

questions.question_text: On a 24-hour schedule, what time is じゅうごじ (jūgoji)?

options.A: 5 p.m.
options.B: 1 p.m.
options.C: 3 p.m.
options.D: 5 a.m.

questions.explanation: じゅうご (jūgo) is 15, and 15:00 is 3 p.m. Subtract 12 from the hour for p.m. times: じゅうはちじ (jūhachiji) is 18:00, i.e. 6 p.m. The 12-hour alternative is ごご さんじ (gogo sanji).

questions.question_text: Compare `つくえの うえに ほんが あります (tsukue no ue ni hon ga arimasu)` with `ほんは つくえの うえに あります (hon wa tsukue no ue ni arimasu)`. When is the second one (with は (wa)) the natural choice?

options.A: When the book is brand-new information
options.B: When the book is a living being
options.C: When you are asking about the time
options.D: When the book is already known to both speakers and you say where it is

questions.explanation: This is the contrast between subject marker が (ga) (introduces something new) and topic marker は (wa) (talks about something already known). Another example: へやに ねこが います (heya ni neko ga imasu) (there is a cat in the room) versus ねこは へやに います (neko wa heya ni imasu) (the cat is in the room).

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.
```text
かばんの なかに なにが ありますか。
(kaban no naka ni nani ga arimasu ka.)
Translation: ____
```

options.A: Where is the bag?
options.B: Whose bag is this?
options.C: Is there a book in the bag?
options.D: What is inside the bag?

questions.explanation: かばんの なかに (kaban no naka ni) means "inside the bag", なにが (nani ga) is "what" as the thing that exists, and ありますか (arimasu ka) asks "is there?".

questions.question_text:
Choose the usual reply.
```text
Child: ただいま。 (tadaima.)
Mother: ____ (____)
```

options.A: いってらっしゃい (itterasshai)
options.B: おかえりなさい (okaeri nasai)
options.C: いただきます (itadakimasu)
options.D: おやすみなさい (oyasumi nasai)

questions.explanation: The fixed pair is ただいま (tadaima) ("I'm back") and おかえりなさい (okaeri nasai) ("welcome back"). The pair for leaving is いってきます (ittekimasu) and いってらっしゃい (itterasshai).

questions.question_text: You made a serious mistake at work and must apologize to your boss. Which apology fits best?

options.A: ごめん (gomen)
options.B: じゃあね (jā ne)
options.C: もうしわけありません (mōshiwake arimasen)
options.D: バイバイ (baibai)

questions.explanation: もうしわけありません (mōshiwake arimasen) is a very formal apology suited to superiors. ごめん (gomen) is too casual, and じゃあね (jā ne) and バイバイ (baibai) are casual goodbyes, not apologies. A middle level is ごめんなさい (gomen nasai) or すみません (sumimasen).

questions.question_text: Two formulas: $\text{country} + jin = \text{nationality}$ and $\text{country} + go = \text{language}$. One result below is NOT a real word because English is an exception. Which one?

options.A: ドイツご (doitsugo)
options.B: イギリスご (igirisugo)
options.C: フランスじん (furansujin)
options.D: にほんじん (nihonjin)

questions.explanation: English is えいご (eigo), not "イギリスご (igirisugo)". The other results are regular: ドイツご (doitsugo) (German), フランスじん (furansujin) (a French person) and にほんじん (nihonjin) (a Japanese person).

questions.question_text:
Fill in the blank: "I speak Portuguese and English."
```text
ポルトガルごと ____ を はなします。
(porutogarugo to ____ o hanashimasu.)
```

options.A: イギリスご (igirisugo)
options.B: えいご (eigo)
options.C: イギリスじん (igirisujin)
options.D: アメリカじん (amerikajin)

questions.explanation: The word for the English language is the irregular えいご (eigo). イギリスじん (igirisujin) and アメリカじん (amerikajin) are nationalities (British and American people), and イギリスご (igirisugo) is not used.

questions.question_text: At the end of an ordinary school day you say goodbye to a classmate you will see again tomorrow. Which farewell is the most natural?

options.A: さようなら (sayōnara)
options.B: またね (mata ne)
options.C: おやすみなさい (oyasumi nasai)
options.D: ただいま (tadaima)

questions.explanation: またね (mata ne) ("see you") is the casual everyday farewell. さようなら (sayōnara) sounds final or like a long separation, おやすみなさい (oyasumi nasai) is only for going to sleep, and ただいま (tadaima) is said on arriving home.

questions.question_text: Why is the English language called えいご (eigo) and not "イギリスご (igirisugo)" (country + ご)?

options.A: English has its own irregular word; the "country + ご" pattern does not apply to it
options.B: Because ご is only used with katakana countries
options.C: Because England has no country name in Japanese
options.D: Because ご is only used for Asian languages

questions.explanation: Most languages follow country + ご (go): ドイツご (doitsugo), フランスご (furansugo), ちゅうごくご (chūgokugo). English is the exception: it is えいご (eigo), even though the country names イギリス (igirisu) and アメリカ (amerika) follow the normal pattern for nationalities.

questions.question_text: Formula: $\text{time} + mae$ means "before" and $\text{time} + sugi$ means "after". How do you say "ten minutes before three"?

options.A: さんじ じゅっぷん まえ (sanji juppun mae)
options.B: さんじ じゅっぷん すぎ (sanji juppun sugi)
options.C: さんじ まえ じゅっぷん (sanji mae juppun)
options.D: じゅっぷん さんじ まえ (juppun sanji mae)

questions.explanation: The time expression comes first and まえ (mae) closes it: さんじ じゅっぷん まえ (sanji juppun mae). With すぎ (sugi) the meaning flips to "ten minutes past three".

questions.question_text: Which clock hours do NOT follow the plain "number + じ (ji)" pattern but have special readings?

options.A: 1, 2 and 3 o'clock
options.B: 10, 11 and 12 o'clock
options.C: 5, 6 and 8 o'clock
options.D: 4, 7 and 9 o'clock

questions.explanation: Most hours are regular, such as いちじ (ichiji) (1), ごじ (goji) (5), ろくじ (rokuji) (6) and はちじ (hachiji) (8). Only 4, 7 and 9 are special: よじ (yoji), しちじ (shichiji) and くじ (kuji), so よんじ (yonji) or ななじ (nanaji) would be mistakes.

questions.question_text: A dish sits right next to the person you are talking to, far from you. Which demonstrative do you use to ask about it?

options.A: これ (kore)
options.B: あれ (are)
options.C: それ (sore)
options.D: どこ (doko)

questions.explanation: The ko-so-a series follows distance: これ (kore) is near the speaker, それ (sore) is near the listener and あれ (are) is far from both. どこ (doko) is "where", not a demonstrative for things.

questions.question_text: Which sentence is correct for "I study every day"?

options.A: まいにち べんきょうします (mainichi benkyō shimasu)
options.B: まいにちに べんきょうします (mainichi ni benkyō shimasu)
options.C: まいにちを べんきょうします (mainichi o benkyō shimasu)
options.D: まいにちが べんきょうします (mainichi ga benkyō shimasu)

questions.explanation: Relative time words (まいにち (mainichi), きょう (kyō), あした (ashita)) take no time particle に (ni); only specific clock times do, as in しちじに おきます (shichiji ni okimasu). This is the rule for the time particle に (ni).

questions.question_text: Origin formula: $\text{place} + kara + kimashita$ ("I came from ..."). Which sentence means "I came from Argentina" (アルゼンチン (aruzenchin))?

options.A: アルゼンチンに きました (aruzenchin ni kimashita)
options.B: アルゼンチンから きました (aruzenchin kara kimashita)
options.C: アルゼンチンまで きました (aruzenchin made kimashita)
options.D: アルゼンチンを きました (aruzenchin o kimashita)

questions.explanation: から (kara) marks the origin. に (ni) would say "I came to Argentina" and まで (made) "I came as far as Argentina".

questions.question_text: Choose the particle: メキシコ ____ すんでいます (mekishiko ____ sunde imasu) ("I live in Mexico").

options.A: に (ni)
options.B: を (o)
options.C: から (kara)
options.D: と (to)

questions.explanation: すんでいます (sunde imasu) (to live) takes に (ni) for the place of residence, the same location particle used for existence. Another example: とうきょうに すんでいます (tōkyō ni sunde imasu) (I live in Tokyo).

questions.question_text: What is the polite negative of これは ケーキです (kore wa kēki desu) ("This is a cake")?

options.A: これは ケーキでは いません (kore wa kēki dewa imasen)
options.B: これは ケーキが ありません (kore wa kēki ga arimasen)
options.C: これは ケーキでは ありません (kore wa kēki dewa arimasen)
options.D: これは ケーキでした (kore wa kēki deshita)

questions.explanation: The negative of です (desu) is では ありません (dewa arimasen) (spoken: じゃ ありません (ja arimasen)). ケーキが ありません (kēki ga arimasen) would mean "there is no cake", and でした (deshita) is past tense. Another example: あれは ピザでは ありません (are wa piza dewa arimasen).

questions.question_text: Plural formula for people: $\text{pronoun} + tachi$. How do you say "we" from わたし (watashi) ("I")?

options.A: わたしじん (watashijin)
options.B: わたしたち (watashitachi)
options.C: わたしご (watashigo)
options.D: わたしの (watashi no)

questions.explanation: たち (tachi) makes pronouns plural: わたしたち (watashitachi) (we) and あなたたち (anatatachi) (you, plural). Do not confuse it with じん (jin) (person of a country) or ご (go) (language).

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.
```text
わたしも コーヒーを ください。
(watashi mo kōhī o kudasai.)
Translation: ____
```

options.A: I do not want coffee, thank you.
options.B: Please give me coffee and tea.
options.C: I would like coffee too, please.
options.D: My coffee is over there.

questions.explanation: も (mo) replaces は (wa) and adds "too": わたしも (watashi mo) is "me too". The rest is the usual request pattern thing + を (o) + ください (kudasai).

questions.question_text: Chained possession: $\text{owner}_1 + no + \text{owner}_2 + no + \text{thing}$. Which phrase means "my friend's umbrella" (かさ (kasa))?

options.A: わたしの ともだちの かさ (watashi no tomodachi no kasa)
options.B: ともだちの わたしの かさ (tomodachi no watashi no kasa)
options.C: かさの ともだちの わたし (kasa no tomodachi no watashi)
options.D: わたしの かさの ともだち (watashi no kasa no tomodachi)

questions.explanation: Each の (no) links a possessor to what follows, so the chain reads from the outermost owner to the thing: my > friend's > umbrella. Reversing it would mean "the umbrella's friend" or similar nonsense.

questions.question_text: Which ending turns a verb such as あいます (aimasu) ("meet") into an invitation, as in "Let's meet tomorrow" (あした あいましょう (ashita aimashō))?

options.A: 〜ません (~masen)
options.B: 〜ました (~mashita)
options.C: 〜ますか (~masu ka)
options.D: 〜ましょう (~mashō)

questions.explanation: The volitional polite ending 〜ましょう (~mashō) means "let's ...". 〜ません (~masen) is negative, 〜ました (~mashita) is past, and 〜ますか (~masu ka) is a plain question. Another example: いっしょに いきましょう (issho ni ikimashō) (let's go together).

questions.question_text: Which is the polite counterpart of the casual apology `ごめん (gomen)`, formed by adding a polite suffix?

options.A: ごめんございます (gomen gozaimasu)
options.B: ごめんます (gomen masu)
options.C: ごめんなさい (gomen nasai)
options.D: ごめんです (gomen desu)

questions.explanation: The polite extension なさい (nasai) is attached to certain casual formulas: ごめん (gomen) > ごめんなさい (gomen nasai) and おやすみ (oyasumi) > おやすみなさい (oyasumi nasai). Others take ございます (gozaimasu), such as おはよう (ohayō) > おはようございます (ohayō gozaimasu).

questions.question_text:
Fill in the blank: "I go back home at 6:30."
```text
ろくじ ____ に うちへ かえります。
(rokuji ____ ni uchi e kaerimasu.)
```

options.A: はん (han)
options.B: ちょうど (chōdo)
options.C: まえ (mae)
options.D: ごご (gogo)

questions.explanation: はん (han) means "half past", so ろくじはん (rokuji han) is 6:30. ちょうど (chōdo) would give 6:00 sharp, and まえ (mae) means "before".

questions.question_text: Why is the greeting こんにちは (konnichiwa) spelled with は (ha/wa) although it is pronounced "wa"?

options.A: こんにちわ (konnichiwa) is an equally correct standard spelling
options.B: は (ha) is always pronounced "wa" at the end of any word
options.C: Greetings are always spelled in katakana, and は is the katakana form
options.D: The は (wa) is a historical spelling of the topic particle, preserved in this fixed greeting

questions.explanation: こんにちは (konnichiwa) comes from a longer phrase meaning roughly "as for today ...", where は (wa) was the topic particle. The spelling stayed, so the standard form is こんにちは (konnichiwa); こんにちわ (konnichiwa) is considered a mistake. The same applies to こんばんは (konbanwa).

questions.question_text:
Complete the minute word for "3 minutes".
```text
さん____
(san____)
```

options.A: ふん (fun)
options.B: ぶん (bun)
options.C: ぷん (pun)
options.D: じ (ji)

questions.explanation: After 3 the counter becomes ぷん (pun): さんぷん (sanpun). The same happens with 1, 4, 6, 8 and 10 (いっぷん (ippun), よんぷん (yonpun), ろっぷん (roppun), はっぷん (happun), じゅっぷん (juppun)), while 2, 5, 7 and 9 keep ふん (fun).

questions.question_text: Which pair of position words are opposites?

options.A: まえ (mae) and となり (tonari)
options.B: なか (naka) and うしろ (ushiro)
options.C: うえ (ue) and した (shita)
options.D: ここ (koko) and そこ (soko)

questions.explanation: うえ (ue) (above) opposes した (shita) (below). The other natural pairs are まえ (mae) (front) and うしろ (ushiro) (behind), and なか (naka) (inside) and そと (soto) (outside). ここ (koko) and そこ (soko) are "here" and "there (near you)".

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.
```text
いま、よじ じゅうごふんです。
(ima, yoji jūgofun desu.)
Translation: ____
```

options.A: It is 4:50 now.
options.B: It is 5:15 now.
options.C: It is 4:05 now.
options.D: It is 4:15 now.

questions.explanation: よじ (yoji) is 4 o'clock and じゅうごふん (jūgofun) is 15 minutes, so the time is 4:15.

questions.question_text: What does `〜ています (~te imasu)` express in `にほんごを べんきょうしています (nihongo o benkyō shite imasu)`?

options.A: A past action: "I studied Japanese"
options.B: An order: "Study Japanese!"
options.C: An action in progress: "I am studying Japanese"
options.D: A negation: "I do not study Japanese"

questions.explanation: This is the te-form + います (imasu) pattern for an ongoing action or state. Another example: ごはんを たべています (gohan o tabete imasu) (I am eating). A past action would be べんきょうしました (benkyō shimashita).

questions.question_text: Listing formula: $A + to + B + o + kudasai$. Which sentence means "Salad and soup, please" (サラダ (sarada), スープ (sūpu))?

options.A: サラダを スープと ください (sarada o sūpu to kudasai)
options.B: サラダと スープと ください (sarada to sūpu to kudasai)
options.C: サラダと スープを ください (sarada to sūpu o kudasai)
options.D: サラダ スープを と ください (sarada sūpu o to kudasai)

questions.explanation: と (to) sits between the two nouns and a single を (o) follows the whole list. Another example: パンと コーヒーを ください (pan to kōhī o kudasai).

questions.question_text: Which word order is correct for "Bread, please"?

options.A: ください パンを (kudasai pan o)
options.B: を パン ください (o pan kudasai)
options.C: パン ください を (pan kudasai o)
options.D: パンを ください (pan o kudasai)

questions.explanation: Japanese is verb-final (subject, object, verb), and a particle always follows the word it marks. So the pattern is thing + を (o) + ください (kudasai). Another example: みずを ください (mizu o kudasai).

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.
```text
わたしの ともだちは フランスじんです。
(watashi no tomodachi wa furansujin desu.)
Translation: ____
```

options.A: My friend speaks French.
options.B: I am a friend of a French person.
options.C: My friend lives in France.
options.D: My friend is French.

questions.explanation: フランスじん (furansujin) means a French person (nationality); the language would be フランスご (furansugo). わたしの ともだち (watashi no tomodachi) is "my friend".

questions.question_text: Sentence formula: $\text{thing} + wa + \text{owner} + no + desu$. Which sentence means "The blue umbrella is his" (blue = あおい (aoi), his = かれの (kare no))?

options.A: かれは あおい かさのです (kare wa aoi kasa no desu)
options.B: あおい かさは かれのです (aoi kasa wa kare no desu)
options.C: あおい かさの かれです (aoi kasa no kare desu)
options.D: あおい かさは かれを です (aoi kasa wa kare o desu)

questions.explanation: The topic あおい かさ (aoi kasa) is followed by は (wa) and by the owner + の (no), where かれの (kare no) stands for "his one" (the noun is dropped). Compare それは わたしのです (sore wa watashi no desu) (that is mine).

questions.question_text: The word きれい (kirei, 'pretty' or 'clean') ends in い (i), yet 'a clean room' is きれいな へや (kirei na heya), not *きれい へや* (kirei heya). What is the best explanation?

options.A: Every adjective that means 'clean' takes な (na), whatever its type
options.B: It is a na-adjective that only looks like an i-adjective, so it needs な (na) before a noun
options.C: It is a noun, so it joins the next noun with の (no), as in きれいの へや (kirei no heya)
options.D: The final い (i) must be replaced by くて (kute) before any noun

questions.explanation: きれい (kirei) is a na-adjective despite its ending, so it needs な (na) directly before a noun: きれいな へや (kirei na heya). A true i-adjective such as あたらしい (atarashii) goes straight in front of the noun: あたらしい くるま (atarashii kuruma). Other look-alikes are ゆうめい (yūmei, famous) and きらい (kirai, disliked): ゆうめいな ひと (yūmei na hito).

questions.question_text: Why is 'green shoes' みどりの くつ (midori no kutsu), while 'red shoes' is あかい くつ (akai kutsu)?

options.A: みどり (midori) is a na-adjective, which is why the particle の (no) replaces な (na)
options.B: Colours that end in り (ri) are verbs, and verbs always take の (no) before a noun
options.C: みどり (midori) is a noun, so it links to the next noun with の (no); あかい (akai) is an i-adjective and stands directly before the noun
options.D: の (no) is a politeness marker added to colours that are hard to pronounce

questions.explanation: Some colours are nouns (みどり midori, ピンク pinku, オレンジ orenji, グレー gurē) and link with の (no): ピンクの てぶくろ (pinku no tebukuro). Colours that end in い (i), such as あかい (akai) and しろい (shiroi), are i-adjectives and attach directly: しろい くつ (shiroi kutsu). Some colours exist in both forms, e.g. しろい くつ (shiroi kutsu) and しろの くつ (shiro no kutsu).

questions.question_text: The adjective あつい (atsui) has several kanji spellings. Which spelling is used for hot tea (a hot drink or object) rather than for hot weather?

options.A: 暑い (atsui)
options.B: 厚い (atsui)
options.C: 冷たい (tsumetai)
options.D: 熱い (atsui)

questions.explanation: 熱い (atsui) describes something hot to the touch or taste, such as tea or a bath. 暑い (atsui) describes hot weather or a hot room. 厚い (atsui) means 'thick', and 冷たい (tsumetai) means 'cold' (for objects). The kana spelling あつい (atsui) is identical, so the kanji (or the context) carries the distinction.

questions.question_text: A learner says 「ぜんぜん にくを たべます」 (zenzen niku o tabemasu) meaning 'I eat meat all the time'. What went wrong?

options.A: ぜんぜん (zenzen) must be paired with a negative verb and means 'not at all'; 'all the time' needs いつも (itsumo) with an affirmative verb
options.B: を (o) must become が (ga) after ぜんぜん (zenzen)
options.C: たべます (tabemasu) can only describe one-off actions, never habits
options.D: ぜんぜん (zenzen) is used only with adjectives, never with verbs

questions.explanation: ぜんぜん (zenzen) and あまり (amari) belong with negative predicates: ぜんぜん にくを たべません (zenzen niku o tabemasen, 'I never eat meat'). For a habit, use an affirmative verb with いつも (itsumo) or まいにち (mainichi): いつも にくを たべます (itsumo niku o tabemasu).

questions.question_text: Someone asks 「さかなが すきじゃ ありませんか」 (sakana ga suki ja arimasen ka, 'Don't you like fish?'). You do not like fish. Which reply is the standard Japanese answer?

options.A: いいえ、すきじゃ ありません (iie, suki ja arimasen)
options.B: はい、すきじゃ ありません (hai, suki ja arimasen)
options.C: はい、すきです (hai, suki desu)
options.D: いいえ、すきです (iie, suki desu)

questions.explanation: In Japanese, はい (hai) confirms the statement inside the question and いいえ (iie) denies it. The question says 'you do not like fish'; since that is true, you answer はい、すきじゃ ありません (hai, suki ja arimasen). Someone who does like fish would deny it with いいえ、すきです (iie, suki desu). Portuguese speakers often invert this because 'sim/não' follows the answer's own polarity.

questions.question_text: Which question word asks 'how many (things)?' and, in casual speech, can also ask a person's age?

options.A: いくら (ikura)
options.B: なんじ (nanji)
options.C: いくつ (ikutsu)
options.D: どこ (doko)

questions.explanation: いくつ (ikutsu) counts items with the native series ひとつ (hitotsu), ふたつ (futatsu)… and also asks age informally; its polite form is おいくつ (oikutsu). いくら (ikura) asks price, なんじ (nanji) asks the time and どこ (doko) asks place. For age with the counter さい (sai), use なんさい (nansai).

questions.question_text: Why is 'He is tall' かれは せが たかいです (kare wa se ga takai desu) rather than just かれは たかいです (kare wa takai desu)?

options.A: Because たかい (takai) is a na-adjective and cannot end a sentence
options.B: Because せ (se) is a polite prefix that must precede every adjective
options.C: Because が (ga) is required between a subject and any i-adjective
options.D: Height is described as 'as for him, the height (せ se) is high' with the は…が (wa … ga) pattern, and plain たかい (takai) would be ambiguous with 'expensive'

questions.explanation: Japanese typically gives the topic (かれ kare) and then says which part or feature has the quality: かれは せが たかいです (kare wa se ga takai desu). The same pattern gives かのじょは かみが ながいです (kanojo wa kami ga nagai desu, 'She has long hair'). たかい (takai) alone could mean 'expensive' or 'high', so naming せ (se, 'height') removes the doubt.

questions.question_text: Which sentence expresses wanting to perform an action, 'I want to buy a souvenir', rather than merely wanting an object?

options.A: おみやげを かいたいです (omiyage o kaitai desu)
options.B: おみやげが ほしいです (omiyage ga hoshii desu)
options.C: おみやげが かいほしいです (omiyage ga kaihoshii desu)
options.D: おみやげを かいます たいです (omiyage o kaimasu tai desu)

questions.explanation: To want an action, attach たい (tai) to the stem of the ます (masu) form: かいます (kaimasu) → かいたい (kaitai). To want a thing, use [thing] が ほしいです ([thing] ga hoshii desu): おみやげが ほしいです (omiyage ga hoshii desu) says 'I want a souvenir', without naming the action. Another example: みずを のみたいです (mizu o nomitai desu, 'I want to drink water').

questions.question_text: Why is 'I go on foot' あるいて いきます (aruite ikimasu), with no で (de), while 'I go by bus' is バスで いきます (basu de ikimasu)?

options.A: で (de) is dropped because あるく (aruku) is an irregular verb
options.B: あるいて (aruite) is the て-form (te-form) of the verb あるく (aruku, 'walk') describing how you go, whereas で (de) attaches to nouns that name a means of transport
options.C: で (de) is only allowed with vehicles that have an engine
options.D: あるいて (aruite) is a noun like バス (basu), and nouns of motion never take で (de)

questions.explanation: で (de) marks the means after a noun: ちかてつで いきます (chikatetsu de ikimasu, 'I go by subway'). 'On foot' is not a noun but a verb in て-form (te-form) joined to the next verb: あるいて いきます (aruite ikimasu). Bicycles are nouns again, so じてんしゃで いきます (jitensha de ikimasu) is correct.

questions.question_text: Someone asks 「えきは どこですか」 (eki wa doko desu ka). The station is visible in the distance, far from both speaker and listener. Which answer fits best?

options.A: ここです (koko desu)
options.B: そこです (soko desu)
options.C: あそこです (asoko desu)
options.D: それです (sore desu)

questions.explanation: The place words follow distance: ここ (koko) is near the speaker, そこ (soko) near the listener, あそこ (asoko) far from both, and どこ (doko) is the question word. それ (sore) is a thing word, not a place. The same triple appears in この／その／あの (kono / sono / ano) before nouns.

questions.question_text: How does Japanese tell 'I eat bread every day' from 'I will eat bread tomorrow' in the polite sentence パンを たべます (pan o tabemasu)?

options.A: Habits use たべます (tabemasu) and the future uses たべるます (taberu masu)
options.B: The future requires を (o) to be doubled
options.C: The verb ending changes depending on who is eating
options.D: The polite non-past form is identical; time words such as まいにち (mainichi) or あした (ashita), plus context, decide the meaning

questions.explanation: The ます (masu) form covers habitual and future actions: まいにち パンを たべます (mainichi pan o tabemasu, 'I eat bread every day') and あした パンを たべます (ashita pan o tabemasu, 'I will eat bread tomorrow'). It also does not change for person or number. Only the past needs a separate form: たべました (tabemashita).

questions.question_text: Why is 'not good' よくない (yokunai) and not *いくない* (ikunai)?

options.A: いい (ii) is a variant of the adjective よい (yoi), and all its conjugated forms are built on the stem よ (yo)
options.B: いい (ii) is a na-adjective, so it needs じゃ ありません (ja arimasen)
options.C: The first い (i) of いい (ii) is a prefix that disappears in negatives
options.D: All adjectives of quality borrow their negative from わるい (warui)

questions.explanation: いい (ii) is the colloquial form of よい (yoi). Only よい (yoi) conjugates, so the negative is よくない (yokunai) and the connective form is よくて (yokute): このかばんは よくて、やすいです (kono kaban wa yokute, yasui desu). Other i-adjectives follow the regular rule, e.g. おおきい (ōkii) → おおきくない (ōkikunai).

questions.question_text: For a cold drink, which adjective is correct, and why is さむい (samui) wrong?

options.A: さむい (samui), because it is the only word for 'cold' in every context
options.B: つめたい (tsumetai), because さむい (samui) describes cold weather or air, not the temperature of an object
options.C: ひくい (hikui), because it means 'low' and applies to drink temperatures
options.D: あたたかい (atatakai), because it means 'slightly cool'

questions.explanation: Japanese separates ambient temperature from the temperature of things: さむい (samui) for weather and rooms, つめたい (tsumetai) for drinks and objects. Likewise あつい (atsui) is written 暑い (atsui) for weather and 熱い (atsui) for hot objects. So 'cold tea' is つめたい おちゃ (tsumetai ocha).

questions.question_text: A written notice says 「これは ほんでは ありません」 (kore wa hon de wa arimasen), while two friends chatting say 「これは ほんじゃ ありません」 (kore wa hon ja arimasen). What is the difference?

options.A: では (de wa) means 'is' and じゃ (ja) means 'is not'
options.B: じゃ (ja) is used with nouns and では (de wa) only with adjectives
options.C: Same meaning ('This is not a book'); では (de wa) is more formal or written, and じゃ (ja) is its spoken contraction
options.D: では (de wa) marks the past tense and じゃ (ja) the present

questions.explanation: では ありません (de wa arimasen) and じゃ ありません (ja arimasen) are both the polite negative of です (desu). では (de wa) is read 'dewa' and suits writing and formal speech; じゃ (ja) is conversational. Another pair: せんせいでは ありません (sensei de wa arimasen) and せんせいじゃ ありません (sensei ja arimasen), 'is not a teacher'.

questions.question_text:
Choose the best translation.
```text
Translation: ____
くろい ぼうしは かるいです。 (kuroi bōshi wa karui desu.)
```

options.A: The black hat is heavy.
options.B: The white hat is light.
options.C: The black hat is expensive.
options.D: The black hat is light.

questions.explanation: くろい (kuroi) is 'black', ぼうし (bōshi) is 'hat' and かるい (karui) is 'light' in weight. The opposite is おもい (omoi, heavy): くろい ぼうしは おもいです (kuroi bōshi wa omoi desu) would be 'The black hat is heavy'.

questions.question_text:
Fill in the blank to say 'pink gloves'.
```text
ピンク ____ てぶくろです。 (pinku ____ tebukuro desu.)
```

options.A: の (no)
options.B: な (na)
options.C: い (i)
options.D: で (de)

questions.explanation: ピンク (pinku) is a loanword that behaves like a noun, so it links to another noun with の (no): ピンクの てぶくろ (pinku no tebukuro). It is not an i-adjective (no *ピンクい* pinkui) and does not take な (na). Similarly オレンジの くつ (orenji no kutsu), 'orange shoes'.

questions.question_text:
Complete the sentence 'This book is not expensive.'
```text
この ほんは たかく ____。 (kono hon wa takaku ____.)
```

options.A: じゃ ありません (ja arimasen)
options.B: ないです (nai desu)
options.C: いです (i desu)
options.D: ません (masen)

questions.explanation: The negative of an i-adjective replaces the final い (i) with くない (kunai) and then adds です (desu): たかい (takai) → たかくないです (takakunai desu). Mixing it with the noun-style ending (*たかくじゃ ありません* takaku ja arimasen) is wrong; the formal alternative is たかくありません (takaku arimasen).

questions.question_text:
Complete the answer.
```text
A: これは ほんですか。 (kore wa hon desu ka.)
B: いいえ、____。 ノートです。 (iie, ____. nōto desu.)
```

options.A: ほんです (hon desu)
options.B: ほんが ありません (hon ga arimasen)
options.C: ほんじゃ ありません (hon ja arimasen)
options.D: ほんを ありません (hon o arimasen)

questions.explanation: The negative of [noun] です ([noun] desu) is [noun] じゃ ありません ([noun] ja arimasen) or では ありません (de wa arimasen): 'It is not a book; it is a notebook.' ありません (arimasen) used with が (ga) would mean 'I do not have a book' and is not an answer to 'Is this a book?'.

questions.question_text:
Fill in the correct question word.
```text
A: あの ひとは ____ ですか。 (ano hito wa ____ desu ka.)
B: わたしの せんせいです。 (watashi no sensei desu.)
```

options.A: なに (nani)
options.B: どこ (doko)
options.C: いくら (ikura)
options.D: だれ (dare)

questions.explanation: The answer 'my teacher' names a person, so the question is あの ひとは だれですか (ano hito wa dare desu ka, 'Who is that person?'). The question word sits exactly where the answer would be. なに／なん (nani / nan) asks about things, どこ (doko) about places and いくら (ikura) about prices.

questions.question_text:
Choose the best translation.

```text
Translation: ____

```

options.A: He is tall and strong.
options.B: He is tall but weak.
options.C: He is short and strong.
options.D: He is tall because he is strong.

questions.explanation: たかくて (takakute) is the connective form of たかい (takai) and simply links two qualities ('tall and …'); it is not 'but' and does not express a reason. せが たかい (se ga takai) is 'tall', つよい (tsuyoi) is 'strong' and よわい (yowai) would be 'weak'.

questions.question_text:

options.B: はたち (hatachi)
options.C: ふたさい (futasai)
options.D: にじゅうつ (nijūtsu)

questions.explanation: Age 20 has its own special word, はたち (hatachi), though にじゅっさい (nijussai) also appears. The counter さい (sai) combines with numbers (さんじゅっさい sanjussai, '30 years old'), but にじさい (nijisai), ふたさい (futasai) and にじゅうつ (nijūtsu) are not used for 20 years old.

questions.question_text:

```text
Translation: ____

```

options.A: I don't want money.
options.B: The money is over there.
options.C: I don't have any money.
options.D: How much is the money?

questions.explanation: あります／ありません (arimasu / arimasen) express existence or possession of things, with the thing marked by が (ga): おかねが ありません (okane ga arimasen). Wanting money would be おかねが ほしいです (okane ga hoshii desu), and a price question uses いくら (ikura).

questions.question_text:
Fill in the verb form.
```text
こうさてんを ____ ください。 (kōsaten o ____ kudasai.)  # Please cross the intersection.
```

options.A: わたります (watarimasu)
options.B: わたる (wataru)
options.C: わたり (watari)
options.D: わたって (watatte)

questions.explanation: A polite request is [verb in て-form (te-form)] + ください (kudasai). わたります (watarimasu) → わたって (watatte), just like まがります (magarimasu) → まがって (magatte). Using the ます (masu) form or the dictionary form before ください (kudasai) is incorrect.

questions.question_text:
Fill in the position word.

```text
ホテルは えきの ____ に あります。 (hoteru wa eki no ____ ni arimasu.)  # The hotel is behind the station.
```
