options.B: まえ (mae)
options.C: となり (tonari)
options.D: ちかく (chikaku)

questions.explanation: Position words follow [reference] の ([reference] no): えきの うしろ (eki no ushiro, behind the station), えきの まえ (eki no mae, in front of), えきの となり (eki no tonari, next to) and えきの ちかく (eki no chikaku, near). Only うしろ (ushiro) means 'behind'.

questions.question_text:
Fill in the verb.
```text
まいにち コーヒーを ____。 (mainichi kōhī o ____.)  # I drink coffee every day.
```

options.A: のみません (nomimasen)
options.B: のみます (nomimasu)
options.C: のみました (nomimashita)
options.D: のみませんでした (nomimasen deshita)

questions.explanation: まいにち (mainichi, 'every day') signals a habit, which uses the polite non-past form: のみます (nomimasu). のみません (nomimasen) is the negative, のみました (nomimashita) the past and のみませんでした (nomimasen deshita) the past negative.

questions.question_text:
Two i-adjectives are linked with the rule $\text{adj} - \text{i} + \text{kute}$ (drop the final i, add kute). Which completion gives 'He is funny and kind'?

`かれは ____ やさしいです。 (kare wa ____ yasashii desu.)` with おもしろい (omoshiroi, 'funny')

options.A: おもしろいくて、(omoshiroikute,)
options.B: おもしろいで、(omoshiroi de,)
options.C: おもしろくて、(omoshirokute,)
options.D: おもしろで、(omoshiro de,)

questions.explanation: Applying $\text{adj} - \text{i} + \text{kute}$ to おもしろい (omoshiroi) gives おもしろくて (omoshirokute): かれは おもしろくて、やさしいです (kare wa omoshirokute, yasashii desu). The final い (i) is replaced, not kept. Na-adjectives and nouns instead take で (de), and いい (ii) becomes よくて (yokute).

questions.question_text: The negative of a wish follows $\text{verb}_{masu} - \text{masu} + \text{takunai} + \text{desu}$. Which form means 'I don't want to buy it' from かいます (kaimasu)?

options.A: かいくないです (kaikunai desu)
options.B: かいたいくないです (kaitaikunai desu)
options.C: かいませんたいです (kaimasen tai desu)
options.D: かいたくないです (kaitakunai desu)

questions.explanation: たい (tai) behaves like an i-adjective, so its negative swaps the final い (i) for くない (kunai): かいたい (kaitai) → かいたくない (kaitakunai), then です (desu) for politeness. Another example: のみたくないです (nomitakunai desu, 'I don't want to drink').

questions.question_text: Descriptions of features follow $\text{person} + \text{wa} + \text{part} + \text{ga} + \text{adj} + \text{desu}$. Which sentence says 'She has short hair' (かのじょ kanojo = she, かみ kami = hair, みじかい mijikai = short)?

options.A: かのじょは かみが みじかいです (kanojo wa kami ga mijikai desu)
options.B: かのじょは かみを みじかいです (kanojo wa kami o mijikai desu)
options.C: かのじょは かみに みじかいです (kanojo wa kami ni mijikai desu)
options.D: かのじょは かみが みじかく です (kanojo wa kami ga mijikaku desu)

questions.explanation: The topic is marked by は (wa), the feature that carries the quality by が (ga), and the adjective plus です (desu) finishes the sentence: かのじょは かみが みじかいです (kanojo wa kami ga mijikai desu). を (o) is for objects of action verbs, and an i-adjective before です (desu) stays in its plain form (not みじかく mijikaku).

questions.question_text: Location answers follow $\text{thing} + \text{wa} + \text{reference} + \text{no} + \text{position} + \text{desu}$. Which sentence says 'The bank is next to the station' (ぎんこう ginkō = bank, えき eki = station, となり tonari = next to)?

options.A: ぎんこうの えきは となりです (ginkō no eki wa tonari desu)
options.B: ぎんこうは えきの となりです (ginkō wa eki no tonari desu)
options.C: ぎんこうは となりの えきです (ginkō wa tonari no eki desu)
options.D: えきは ぎんこうの となりです (eki wa ginkō no tonari desu)

questions.explanation: In the formula, the located thing is the topic (ぎんこう ginkō), then the reference point with の (no), then the position word. The mirror image えきは ぎんこうの となりです (eki wa ginkō no tonari desu) places the station next to the bank, which is a different statement. Compare: ホテルは えきの まえです (hoteru wa eki no mae desu), 'The hotel is in front of the station'.

questions.question_text: Possession chains follow $N_1 + \text{no} + N_2 + \text{no} + N_3$, where the possessor comes first. Which phrase means 'Mr. Tanaka's friend's bag'?

options.A: かばんの ともだちの たなかさん (kaban no tomodachi no Tanaka-san)
options.B: ともだちの たなかさんの かばん (tomodachi no Tanaka-san no kaban)
options.C: たなかさんの ともだちの かばん (Tanaka-san no tomodachi no kaban)
options.D: たなかさんが ともだちが かばん (Tanaka-san ga tomodachi ga kaban)

questions.explanation: の (no) links two nouns with the 'owner' on the left and the 'owned' on the right, and it can be chained: たなかさんの ともだち (Tanaka-san no tomodachi, 'Mr. Tanaka's friend') + の かばん (no kaban). Reversing the order gives 'the bag's friend's Mr. Tanaka'. The same pattern appears in わたしの ちず (watashi no chizu, 'my map').

questions.question_text: Chaining a na-adjective and an i-adjective follows $\text{na-adj} + \text{de}, \ \text{i-adj} + \text{desu}$. Which sentence says 'The room is clean and big' (きれい kirei = clean, おおきい ōkii = big)?

options.A: へやは きれいくて、おおきいです (heya wa kireikute, ōkii desu)
options.B: へやは きれいな、おおきいです (heya wa kirei na, ōkii desu)
options.C: へやは きれいと おおきいです (heya wa kirei to ōkii desu)
options.D: へやは きれいで、おおきいです (heya wa kirei de, ōkii desu)

questions.explanation: A na-adjective (and a noun) links to what follows with で (de), so きれい (kirei) becomes きれいで (kirei de). The くて (kute) ending is only for i-adjectives, and な (na) is only used right before a noun. Another example: しずかで、あかるいです (shizuka de, akarui desu), 'It is quiet and bright'.

questions.question_text: Frequency with a negative verb follows $\text{amari} + \text{object} + \text{o} + \text{verb}_{masen}$ ('not very often'). Which sentence says 'I don't drink alcohol very often' (おさけ osake = alcohol)?

options.A: あまり おさけを のみません (amari osake o nomimasen)
options.B: あまり おさけを のみます (amari osake o nomimasu)
options.C: ぜんぜん おさけを のみます (zenzen osake o nomimasu)
options.D: ぜんぜん おさけを のみません (zenzen osake o nomimasen)

questions.explanation: あまり (amari) needs a negative verb and means 'not very (often)': あまり おさけを のみません (amari osake o nomimasen). ぜんぜん おさけを のみません (zenzen osake o nomimasen) is stronger: 'I never drink alcohol'. Both words require the ません (masen) form; an affirmative verb after them is ungrammatical.

questions.question_text: A polite request follows $\text{verb}_{te} + \text{kudasai}$. The て-form (te-form) of いきます (ikimasu, 'go') is irregular. Which sentence means 'Please go straight'?

options.A: まっすぐ いきて ください (massugu ikite kudasai)
options.B: まっすぐ いって ください (massugu itte kudasai)
options.C: まっすぐ いいて ください (massugu iite kudasai)
options.D: まっすぐ いきます ください (massugu ikimasu kudasai)

questions.explanation: For verbs whose dictionary form ends in く (ku), the て-form (te-form) normally becomes いて (ite), but いく (iku) is the exception and gives いって (itte). So いって ください (itte kudasai) means 'please go'. Regular patterns also exist: まがります (magarimasu) → まがって (magatte), みます (mimasu) → みて (mite).

questions.question_text: The negative of ほしい (hoshii, 'want [a thing]') follows $\text{thing} + \text{ga} + \text{hoshikunai} + \text{desu}$. Which sentence says 'I don't want a souvenir' (おみやげ omiyage = souvenir)?

options.A: おみやげを ほしくないです (omiyage o hoshikunai desu)
options.B: おみやげが ほしいくないです (omiyage ga hoshiikunai desu)
options.C: おみやげが ほしくないです (omiyage ga hoshikunai desu)
options.D: おみやげが ほしくありませんです (omiyage ga hoshiku arimasen desu)

questions.explanation: ほしい (hoshii) is an i-adjective, so its negative replaces the final い (i) with くない (kunai): ほしくない (hoshikunai). The wanted thing takes が (ga): おみやげが ほしくないです (omiyage ga hoshikunai desu). Mixing endings, as in ほしくありませんです (hoshiku arimasen desu), is wrong; the formal pattern is ほしくありません (hoshiku arimasen).

questions.question_text: Past negative of a noun sentence follows $\text{N} + \text{de wa} + \text{arimasen} + \text{deshita}$. Which sentence says 'It was not a book'?

options.A: ほんでは ありました (hon de wa arimashita)
options.B: ほんでは ありませんです (hon de wa arimasen desu)
options.C: ほんでした ではありません (hon deshita de wa arimasen)
options.D: ほんでは ありませんでした (hon de wa arimasen deshita)

questions.explanation: The polite present negative ほんでは ありません (hon de wa arimasen) becomes past by adding でした (deshita): ほんでは ありませんでした (hon de wa arimasen deshita). The spoken variant is ほんじゃ ありませんでした (hon ja arimasen deshita). For verbs the past negative is similar: たべませんでした (tabemasen deshita).

questions.question_text: Wishes with a destination follow $\text{place} + \text{e} + \text{verb stem} + \text{tai desu}$. Which sentence says 'I want to go to the hotel'?

options.A: ホテルへ いきたいです (hoteru e ikitai desu)
options.B: ホテルを いきたいです (hoteru o ikitai desu)
options.C: ホテルで いきたいです (hoteru de ikitai desu)
options.D: ホテルへ いきます たいです (hoteru e ikimasu tai desu)

questions.explanation: The direction particle へ (e, written he) marks the destination, and the stem of いきます (ikimasu) plus たいです (tai desu) gives いきたいです (ikitai desu). で (de) marks means or place of action, not destination. Another example: くうこうへ いきたいです (kūkō e ikitai desu), 'I want to go to the airport'.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says 'I like fish'?

options.A: わたしは さかなを すきです (watashi wa sakana o suki desu)
options.B: わたしは さかなが すきです (watashi wa sakana ga suki desu)
options.C: わたしは さかなに すきです (watashi wa sakana ni suki desu)
options.D: わたしは さかなで すきです (watashi wa sakana de suki desu)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: が (ga) marks the object of liking with すき／きらい (suki / kirai). These words work like adjectives, so the thing liked is marked with が (ga), not を (o), which is reserved for objects of action verbs. Another example: わたしは カレーが だいすきです (watashi wa karē ga daisuki desu), 'I love curry'.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says 'Ken is quiet and serious' (しずか shizuka = quiet and まじめ majime = serious are both na-adjectives)?

options.A: けんさんは しずかくて、まじめです (Ken-san wa shizukakute, majime desu)
options.B: けんさんは しずかな、まじめです (Ken-san wa shizuka na, majime desu)
options.C: けんさんは しずかで、まじめです (Ken-san wa shizuka de, majime desu)
options.D: けんさんは しずかに、まじめです (Ken-san wa shizuka ni, majime desu)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: linking na-adjectives with で (de). A na-adjective connects to the next predicate with で (de), while くて (kute) is for i-adjectives and な (na) only appears before a noun. Another example: マリアさんは きれいで、かしこいです (Maria-san wa kirei de, kashikoi desu), 'Maria is pretty and clever'.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says 'She is a teacher and kind'?

options.A: かのじょは せんせいくて、やさしいです (kanojo wa senseikute, yasashii desu)
options.B: かのじょは せんせいの、やさしいです (kanojo wa sensei no, yasashii desu)
options.C: かのじょは せんせいな、やさしいです (kanojo wa sensei na, yasashii desu)
options.D: かのじょは せんせいで、やさしいです (kanojo wa sensei de, yasashii desu)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: noun + で (de) to link a noun to a following predicate. After a noun, で (de) plays the role of 'and' in sequences: せんせいで、やさしいです (sensei de, yasashii desu). くて (kute) is only for i-adjectives. Another example: ともだちは いしゃで、いそがしいです (tomodachi wa isha de, isogashii desu), 'My friend is a doctor and busy'.

questions.question_text: Which form correctly says 'This coat is not cheap' (やすい yasui = cheap)?

options.A: このコートは やすくないです (kono kōto wa yasukunai desu)
options.B: このコートは やすいじゃ ありません (kono kōto wa yasui ja arimasen)
options.C: このコートは やすいではありません (kono kōto wa yasui de wa arimasen)
options.D: このコートは やすないです (kono kōto wa yasunai desu)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: negative of i-adjectives. Replace the final い (i) with くない (kunai) and add です (desu): やすい (yasui) → やすくないです (yasukunai desu). The じゃ ありません (ja arimasen) pattern is for nouns and na-adjectives, not i-adjectives. Another example: おおきくないです (ōkikunai desu), 'It isn't big'.

questions.question_text: Which form correctly says 'This town is not quiet' (しずか shizuka = quiet)?

options.A: このまちは しずかくないです (kono machi wa shizukakunai desu)
options.B: このまちは しずかじゃ ありません (kono machi wa shizuka ja arimasen)
options.C: このまちは しずかないです (kono machi wa shizuka nai desu)
options.D: このまちは しずかなじゃ ありません (kono machi wa shizuka na ja arimasen)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: negative of na-adjectives. They use the noun pattern: stem + じゃ ありません (ja arimasen) or では ありません (de wa arimasen), with no な (na). くない (kunai) is only for i-adjectives. Another example: このへやは きれいじゃ ありません (kono heya wa kirei ja arimasen), 'This room is not clean'.

questions.question_text:
Which word completes 'This bag is heavy'?

`____ かばんは おもいです。 (____ kaban wa omoi desu.)`

options.A: これ (kore)
options.B: ここ (koko)
options.C: この (kono)
options.D: あれ (are)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: demonstrative modifiers この／その／あの (kono / sono / ano) versus pronouns これ／それ／あれ (kore / sore / are). A pronoun stands in for the noun, while この (kono) must be followed by a noun: この かばん (kono kaban). Saying *これ かばん* (kore kaban) is a typical error. Another example: あの くつは たかいです (ano kutsu wa takai desu).

questions.question_text:
Which particle pair completes 'I go to the airport by subway'?

`ちかてつ ( 1 ) くうこう ( 2 ) いきます。 (chikatetsu ( 1 ) kūkō ( 2 ) ikimasu.)`

options.B: 1 = に (ni), 2 = で (de)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: で (de) for means and へ (e) for direction. The means of transport takes で (de) and the destination takes へ (e, written he) or に (ni): ちかてつで くうこうへ いきます (chikatetsu de kūkō e ikimasu). Another example: バスで えきへ いきます (basu de eki e ikimasu), 'I go to the station by bus'.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly asks someone politely, 'Please turn right'?

options.A: みぎに まがって ください (migi ni magatte kudasai)
options.B: みぎに まがります ください (migi ni magarimasu kudasai)
options.C: みぎに まがる ください (migi ni magaru kudasai)
options.D: みぎに まがりて ください (migi ni magarite kudasai)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: request with the て-form (te-form) + ください (kudasai). Verbs ending in る (ru) like まがる (magaru) change to って (tte): まがって (magatte). Neither the ます (masu) form nor the dictionary form can precede ください (kudasai). Another example: ひだりに まがって ください (hidari ni magatte kudasai), 'Please turn left'.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says 'At lunch I eat fish'?

options.A: ひるごはんを さかなに たべます (hirugohan o sakana ni tabemasu)
options.B: ひるごはんに さかなを たべます (hirugohan ni sakana o tabemasu)
options.C: ひるごはんが さかなを たべます (hirugohan ga sakana o tabemasu)
options.D: ひるごはんと さかなが たべます (hirugohan to sakana ga tabemasu)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: に (ni) marking the time or meal at which an action happens, and を (o) marking the object, with the verb last. ひるごはんに (hirugohan ni) says 'at lunch', さかなを (sakana o) 'fish' as the thing eaten. Another example: あさごはんに たまごを たべます (asagohan ni tamago o tabemasu), 'At breakfast I eat eggs'.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says 'I did not drink coffee yesterday' (きのう kinō = yesterday)?

options.A: きのう コーヒーを のみましたません (kinō kōhī o nomimashitamasen)
options.B: きのう コーヒーを のみませんです (kinō kōhī o nomimasen desu)
options.C: きのう コーヒーを のみませんでした (kinō kōhī o nomimasen deshita)
options.D: きのう コーヒーを のみないでした (kinō kōhī o nominai deshita)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: past negative polite form ～ませんでした (~masen deshita). Take the polite negative のみません (nomimasen) and add でした (deshita). The past affirmative is のみました (nomimashita). Another example: パンを たべませんでした (pan o tabemasen deshita), 'I did not eat bread'.

questions.question_text: Which noun phrase correctly means 'a big, red bag' (おおきい ōkii = big, あかい akai = red, かばん kaban = bag) when the two adjectives are linked with the connective form?

options.A: おおきいな あかい かばん (ōkii na akai kaban)
options.B: おおきいで あかい かばん (ōkii de akai kaban)
options.C: おおきいです あかい かばん (ōkii desu akai kaban)
options.D: おおきくて あかい かばん (ōkikute akai kaban)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: the connective form くて (kute) of an i-adjective. Dropping the final い (i) and adding くて (kute) links the adjective to the next one: おおきくて あかい (ōkikute akai). な (na) is for na-adjectives, で (de) for nouns and na-adjectives, and です (desu) cannot appear inside a noun phrase. Another example: ながくて くろい かみ (nagakute kuroi kami), 'long, black hair'.

questions.question_text: Which question correctly asks 'What do you eat for breakfast?'

options.A: あさごはんに なにを たべますか (asagohan ni nani o tabemasu ka)
options.B: あさごはんに なにが たべますか (asagohan ni nani ga tabemasu ka)
options.C: たべますか あさごはんに なにを (tabemasu ka asagohan ni nani o)
options.D: あさごはんを なにに たべますか (asagohan o nani ni tabemasu ka)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: question words keep the particle and position of the answer, and the verb plus か (ka) comes last. The answer would be パンを たべます (pan o tabemasu), so the question word takes を (o): なにを (nani o). Putting the verb first breaks Japanese word order. Another example: なにを のみますか (nani o nomimasu ka), 'What do you drink?'

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says 'The hotel is near the station'?

options.A: ホテルは えきを ちかくに あります (hoteru wa eki o chikaku ni arimasu)
options.B: ホテルは えきの ちかくに あります (hoteru wa eki no chikaku ni arimasu)
options.C: ホテルは えきで ちかくに あります (hoteru wa eki de chikaku ni arimasu)
options.D: ホテルは えきに ちかくの あります (hoteru wa eki ni chikaku no arimasu)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: [reference] の [position] に あります ([reference] no [position] ni arimasu) for location. の (no) joins the reference noun to the position word, and に (ni) marks where something exists with あります (arimasu). Another example: コンビニは ホテルの まえに あります (konbini wa hoteru no mae ni arimasu), 'The convenience store is in front of the hotel'.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says 'He is quiet, but funny'?

options.A: かれは しずかですから、おもしろいです (kare wa shizuka desu kara, omoshiroi desu)
options.B: かれは しずかですと、おもしろいです (kare wa shizuka desu to, omoshiroi desu)
options.C: かれは しずかですが、おもしろいです (kare wa shizuka desu ga, omoshiroi desu)
options.D: かれは しずかですを、おもしろいです (kare wa shizuka desu o, omoshiroi desu)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: が (ga) as the contrast conjunction 'but' after a clause ending in です (desu) or ます (masu). から (kara) means 'because', so it changes the logic to 'He is quiet, so he is funny'. A separate sentence with でも (demo) also works: かれは しずかです。でも、おもしろいです (kare wa shizuka desu. Demo, omoshiroi desu).

questions.question_text: A learner keeps writing *きれい へや* (kirei heya) and *ゆうめい ひと* (yūmei hito), missing the な (na). Which study strategy fixes this most reliably?

options.A: Always add な (na) after every adjective ending in い (i), just to be safe
options.B: Avoid adjectives before nouns and only use [noun] は [adjective] です ([noun] wa [adjective] desu) sentences
options.C: Memorise only the English meaning, because the adjective type follows from the meaning
options.D: Learn the troublemakers (きれい kirei, ゆうめい yūmei, きらい kirai) as whole chunks with a noun, e.g. きれいな へや (kirei na heya), and contrast them with true i-adjectives such as おいしい (oishii)

questions.explanation: The adjective type is a property of each word, not of its meaning or its ending, and a small set of na-adjectives end in い (i). Storing the troublemakers as ready-made phrases (きれいな へや kirei na heya, ゆうめいな ひと yūmei na hito) and testing them against look-alike i-adjectives builds the right reflex. Adding な (na) everywhere would produce errors like *おいしいな ケーキ* (oishii na kēki).

questions.question_text: In casual conversation you hear 「パンを たべます」 (pan o tabemasu) without any subject. How should a learner interpret who is eating?

options.A: The verb does not mark person, so the subject comes from context; by default a statement is about the speaker and a question about the listener
options.B: It is always third person, because first person requires わたしは (watashi wa)
options.C: The ending ます (masu) signals that the speaker is the subject
options.D: The sentence is ungrammatical without an explicit subject

questions.explanation: Japanese drops any element that is clear from context, including subjects. Because verbs like たべます (tabemasu) do not change for person or number, the subject is inferred: パンを たべます (pan o tabemasu) normally means 'I eat bread', while パンを たべますか (pan o tabemasu ka) asks about you. Adding わたしは (watashi wa) is only needed for contrast or clarity.

questions.question_text: Someone asks 「だれが やさしいですか」 (dare ga yasashii desu ka, 'Who is kind?'). Which answer is most natural, and why?

options.A: ともだちを やさしいです (tomodachi o yasashii desu), because answers always take を (o)
options.B: ともだちが やさしいです (tomodachi ga yasashii desu), because the new information that answers the question word is marked with が (ga)
options.C: ともだちの やさしいです (tomodachi no yasashii desu), because の (no) replaces the question word
options.D: ともだちで やさしいです (tomodachi de yasashii desu), because で (de) marks the answer to 'who'

questions.explanation: When a question word is the subject (だれが dare ga), the answer fills the same slot with が (ga): ともだちが やさしいです (tomodachi ga yasashii desu). The topic marker は (wa) is for information already established, as in ともだちは やさしいです (tomodachi wa yasashii desu). を (o) belongs to the objects of action verbs, and の (no) and で (de) do not mark subjects.

questions.question_text: A tourist must ask a stranger where the station is. Which version combines the right politeness level and structure?

options.A: おい、えき どこ (oi, eki doko)
options.B: えきは どこだ (eki wa doko da)
options.C: すみません、えきは どこですか (sumimasen, eki wa doko desu ka)
options.D: きみ、えきは どこ (kimi, eki wa doko)

questions.explanation: With strangers, use the polite です (desu) / ます (masu) style and open with an attention-getter like すみません (sumimasen): すみません、えきは どこですか (sumimasen, eki wa doko desu ka). Plain forms (どこだ doko da), bare nouns (えき どこ eki doko) and blunt calls (おい oi, きみ kimi) sound rude or too familiar. Another polite example: すみません、トイレは どこですか (sumimasen, toire wa doko desu ka).

questions.question_text: You want to ask the age of an older stranger as politely as possible. Which question is best?

options.A: なんさいだ (nansai da)
options.B: いくつ (ikutsu)
options.C: なんさい (nansai)
options.D: おいくつですか (oikutsu desu ka)

questions.explanation: おいくつですか (oikutsu desu ka) uses the honorific お (o) with いくつ (ikutsu) plus polite ですか (desu ka), so it is the courteous way to ask an adult's age. なんさいですか (nansai desu ka) is fine for children or peers, but plain なんさい (nansai) or いくつ (ikutsu) without ですか (desu ka), or なんさいだ (nansai da), sound abrupt.

questions.question_text: A learner builds 'an expensive bag' as 「たかいです かばん」 (takai desu kaban). Which diagnosis and fix are right?

options.A: です (desu) ends a sentence and cannot stand between an adjective and the noun it modifies; the fix is たかい かばん (takai kaban)
options.B: Replace です (desu) with な (na): たかいな かばん (takai na kaban)
options.C: Add の (no): たかいです の かばん (takai desu no kaban)
options.D: Nothing; the phrase is correct and extra polite

questions.explanation: An i-adjective placed before a noun stays in its plain form with no です (desu): たかい かばん (takai kaban). です (desu) belongs at the end of a predicate: この かばんは たかいです (kono kaban wa takai desu). Similarly あかい かばんです (akai kaban desu) puts です (desu) only after the whole phrase.

questions.question_text: Someone asks 「どんな ひとですか」 (donna hito desu ka) about your friend. Which answer actually answers the question?

options.A: たなかさんです (Tanaka-san desu)
options.B: おもしろい ひとです (omoshiroi hito desu)
options.C: にじゅっさいです (nijussai desu)
options.D: あそこです (asoko desu)

questions.explanation: どんな (donna) means 'what kind of' and asks for a description (personality, appearance). A name answers だれ (dare), an age answers なんさい (nansai) and a place answers どこ (doko). Another example: どんな まちですか (donna machi desu ka) is answered with しずかな まちです (shizuka na machi desu).

questions.question_text: At a market you want to know how many apples there are. Which question is correct?

options.A: りんごは いくら ありますか (ringo wa ikura arimasu ka)
options.B: りんごは なんさい ありますか (ringo wa nansai arimasu ka)
options.C: りんごは いくつ ありますか (ringo wa ikutsu arimasu ka)
options.D: りんごは だれ ありますか (ringo wa dare arimasu ka)

questions.explanation: いくつ (ikutsu) asks 'how many' for ordinary objects (the native counting series ひとつ hitotsu, ふたつ futatsu, …). いくら (ikura) asks price, なんさい (nansai) asks age with the counter さい (sai), and だれ (dare) asks 'who'. So りんごは いくつ ありますか (ringo wa ikutsu arimasu ka) asks for a quantity.

questions.question_text: Why does a Brazilian learner who writes 「さかなを すきです」 (sakana o suki desu) make a systematic mistake, and which approach prevents it?

options.A: すき (suki) is a verb of action, so を (o) is right and が (ga) is a typo
options.B: Japanese has no particle for the thing liked, so the particle is simply dropped
options.C: Always use は (wa) instead of any other particle with feelings
options.D: すき (suki) is adjective-like, so its object takes が (ga); memorise [thing] が すきです ([thing] ga suki desu) as a pattern instead of translating 'gostar de' word by word

questions.explanation: Portuguese 'gostar de' is verb-like, and learners carry that over by choosing を (o). Japanese treats すき (suki) and きらい (kirai) as na-adjectives, and the liked thing takes が (ga): さかなが すきです (sakana ga suki desu). Learning the whole frame prevents word-by-word translation. The same frame covers ほしい (hoshii): ちずが ほしいです (chizu ga hoshii desu).

questions.question_text: At a shop counter you want a map. Which wording is the most natural direct request, and why?

options.A: ちずを ください (chizu o kudasai): ください (kudasai) asks the other person to hand it over, while ほしいです (hoshii desu) only reports your own wish
options.B: ちずが ほしいです (chizu ga hoshii desu): ください (kudasai) is reserved for restaurants
options.C: ちずを ほしいです (chizu o hoshii desu): ほしい (hoshii) takes を (o) when talking to staff
options.D: ちずです (chizu desu): naming only the item is the polite way to ask

questions.explanation: [thing] を ください ([thing] o kudasai) is the standard polite request for receiving something: ちずを ください (chizu o kudasai), パスポートを ください (pasupōto o kudasai). ほしいです (hoshii desu) states desire and is more of an observation about yourself, typically after asking for information such as ちずは ありますか (chizu wa arimasu ka).

questions.question_text: A Brazilian translates 'tenho 25 anos' as 「わたしは にじゅうごさいを もっています」 (watashi wa nijūgosai o motte imasu). What is the right way to think about stating age in Japanese?

options.A: Replace もっています (motte imasu) with あります (arimasu): にじゅうごさいが あります (nijūgosai ga arimasu)
options.B: Age is a state expressed with です (desu) and the counter さい (sai): わたしは にじゅうごさいです (watashi wa nijūgosai desu); there is no 'have' verb for age
options.C: Use ほしい (hoshii): にじゅうごさいが ほしいです (nijūgosai ga hoshii desu)
options.D: The sentence is fine; polite speakers prefer 'having' an age

questions.explanation: Japanese states age as an identity: [person] は [number] さいです ([person] wa [number] sai desu). The Portuguese 'ter' (have) does not translate. 25 is にじゅうご (nijūgo), so にじゅうごさい (nijūgosai). Another example: ともだちは さんじゅっさいです (tomodachi wa sanjussai desu), 'My friend is 30'.

questions.question_text: Which practice drill best consolidates the four polite verb forms (affirmative, negative, past, past negative)?

options.A: Copy each form ten times in kana without ever combining it with a sentence
options.B: Read a list of 100 verbs in dictionary form only
options.C: Take one sentence such as パンを たべます (pan o tabemasu) and say it in all four forms: たべます (tabemasu), たべません (tabemasen), たべました (tabemashita), たべませんでした (tabemasen deshita)
options.D: Memorise only the negative, since the other forms can be derived from it

questions.explanation: Transformation drills keep the object, particle and context constant while only the ending changes, which makes the contrast between ます (masu), ません (masen), ました (mashita) and ませんでした (masen deshita) visible and forces production. Passive copying or reading one form does not train retrieval. The pattern also transfers: のみます (nomimasu) → のみませんでした (nomimasen deshita).

questions.question_text: In 「これは ほんです」 (kore wa hon desu), the topic particle is spelled with は (ha). Which statement is correct?

options.A: It is written わ (wa) because particles always use the spoken kana
options.B: It is pronounced 'ha' because spelling decides pronunciation
options.C: It is pronounced 'o' because all particles share one sound
options.D: It is written は (ha) but pronounced 'wa' when it is a particle, which is why rōmaji shows 'kore wa'

questions.explanation: A few particles keep historical spellings: は (written ha) is read 'wa', へ (written he) is read 'e', and を (o) is read 'o'. Reading rōmaji alone can hide these spellings, so learners should connect particle sounds to their kana early. Another example: くうこうへ いきます (kūkō e ikimasu), where へ is written he but spoken e.

questions.question_text: You want to say 'I don't eat fish very often' (sometimes you do), not 'I never eat fish'. Which sentence is the most accurate?

options.A: さかなを あまり たべません (sakana o amari tabemasen)
options.B: さかなを ぜんぜん たべません (sakana o zenzen tabemasen)
options.C: さかなを いつも たべません (sakana o itsumo tabemasen)
options.D: さかなを よく たべます (sakana o yoku tabemasu)

questions.explanation: あまり～ません (amari ~ masen) means 'not very often/much', leaving room for exceptions. ぜんぜん～ません (zenzen ~ masen) means 'not at all / never', which is stronger. よく たべます (yoku tabemasu) says you eat it often, the opposite. Choosing the adverb is therefore a choice of frequency, not just of grammar.

questions.question_text:
Choose the best translation.
```text
Translation: ____
わたしの ともだちは しずかで、おもしろい ひとです。
(watashi no tomodachi wa shizuka de, omoshiroi hito desu.)
```

options.A: My friend is quiet but not interesting.
options.B: My friend is a quiet and interesting person.
options.C: My quiet friend is in an interesting place.
options.D: My friends are quiet because they are funny.

questions.explanation: しずかで (shizuka de) links the na-adjective 'quiet' to what follows as 'quiet and …', and おもしろい ひと (omoshiroi hito) is 'an interesting person'. The sentence contains no word for 'but' or 'because' (those would be が ga / でも demo and から kara).

questions.question_text:
Choose the pair of particles that completes the dialogue.
```text
A: すみません、ぎんこうは どこ ____(1) ありますか。
   (sumimasen, ginkō wa doko ____(1) arimasu ka.)
B: えきの となり ____(2) あります。
   (eki no tonari ____(2) arimasu.)
```

options.A: 1 = で (de), 2 = で (de)
options.C: 1 = に (ni), 2 = に (ni)

questions.explanation: あります (arimasu) states that something exists somewhere, and the place of existence takes に (ni): どこに ありますか (doko ni arimasu ka), となりに あります (tonari ni arimasu). で (de) marks where an action takes place, as in レストランで たべます (resutoran de tabemasu).

questions.question_text:
Complete the answer.
```text
A: ちずは ありますか。 (chizu wa arimasu ka.)  # Do you have maps?
B: いいえ、____。 (iie, ____.)
```

options.A: いません (imasen)
options.B: ありませんです (arimasen desu)
options.C: あるません (arumasen)
options.D: ありません (arimasen)

questions.explanation: The polite negative of あります (arimasu) is ありません (arimasen). います／いません (imasu / imasen) are used for living beings, not objects like maps. Forms like ありませんです (arimasen desu) and あるません (arumasen) do not exist. Another example: おかねが ありません (okane ga arimasen), 'I have no money'.

questions.question_text:
Complete the answer.
```text
A: そのレストランは おいしいですか。 (sono resutoran wa oishii desu ka.)
B: いいえ、あまり ____。 (iie, amari ____.)  # No, not very tasty.
```

options.A: おいしくないです (oishikunai desu)
options.B: おいしいくないです (oishiikunai desu)
options.C: おいしじゃ ありません (oishi ja arimasen)
options.D: おいしいです (oishii desu)

questions.explanation: あまり (amari) requires a negative predicate. The negative of an i-adjective replaces the final い (i) with くない (kunai): おいしい (oishii) → おいしくないです (oishikunai desu). The じゃ ありません (ja arimasen) pattern is for nouns and na-adjectives, and the affirmative おいしいです (oishii desu) cannot follow あまり (amari).

questions.question_text:
Complete the question.
```text
このバスは えき ____ いきますか。 (kono basu wa eki ____ ikimasu ka.)  # Does this bus go to the station?
```

options.A: で (de)
options.B: へ (e)
options.C: が (ga)
options.D: の (no)

questions.explanation: The direction or destination of a movement verb takes へ (e, written he) or に (ni): えきへ いきますか (eki e ikimasu ka). で (de) would mark a means or location of action, and が (ga) or の (no) cannot mark destinations. Another example: ホテルへ きます (hoteru e kimasu), 'I come to the hotel'.

questions.question_text:
Choose the best translation.
```text
Translation: ____
かれは あまり しずかじゃ ありません。 (kare wa amari shizuka ja arimasen.)
```

options.A: He is very quiet.
options.B: He is never quiet.
options.C: He is not very quiet.
options.D: He is a little quiet.

questions.explanation: あまり (amari) plus a negative means 'not very'. So しずかじゃ ありません (shizuka ja arimasen) with あまり (amari) is 'is not very quiet'. 'Very quiet' would be とても しずかです (totemo shizuka desu), 'a little quiet' すこし しずかです (sukoshi shizuka desu), and 'never/not at all' would use ぜんぜん (zenzen).

questions.question_text:
Choose the pair of particles.
```text
わたしは さかな ____(1) たべません が、にく ____(2) だいすきです。
(watashi wa sakana ____(1) tabemasen ga, niku ____(2) daisuki desu.)
```

options.C: 1 = が (ga), 2 = が (ga)

questions.explanation: Action verbs like たべません (tabemasen) mark their object with を (o): さかなを たべません (sakana o tabemasen). Feelings such as だいすき (daisuki) mark the thing with が (ga): にくが だいすきです (niku ga daisuki desu). The conjunction が (ga) after たべません (tabemasen) means 'but' and is a different function of the same sound.

questions.question_text:
Choose the best translation.
```text
Translation: ____
かのじょは きれいで、せが たかいです。 (kanojo wa kirei de, se ga takai desu.)
```

options.A: She is pretty and tall.
options.B: She is pretty but short.
options.C: She is tall and her room is clean.
options.D: She is clean because she is expensive.

questions.explanation: きれいで (kirei de) links a na-adjective as 'pretty and …' (きれい also means 'clean' for things), and せが たかい (se ga takai) is 'tall'. Note that たかい (takai) alone could mean 'expensive', which is why the height is named with せ (se).

questions.question_text:
Fill in the question word.
```text
A: ____ が すきですか。 (____ ga suki desu ka.)
B: カレーが すきです。 (karē ga suki desu.)
```

options.A: どこ (doko)
options.B: なに (nani)
options.C: いつ (itsu)
options.D: いくら (ikura)

questions.explanation: The answer names a food, so the question asks 'what': なにが すきですか (nani ga suki desu ka, 'What do you like?'). The question word keeps the particle of the answer, here が (ga). どこ (doko) asks place, いつ (itsu) time and いくら (ikura) price.

questions.question_text:
Choose the best translation.
```text
Translation: ____
ひるごはんに さかなを たべませんでした。
(hirugohan ni sakana o tabemasen deshita.)
```

options.A: I don't eat fish at lunch.
options.B: I ate fish at lunch.
options.C: I did not eat fish at lunch.
options.D: I won't eat fish for lunch.

questions.explanation: ～ませんでした (~masen deshita) is the polite past negative, so the sentence is 'did not eat'. The non-past negative would be たべません (tabemasen), the past affirmative たべました (tabemashita), and a future plan uses たべます (tabemasu) with a time word. ひるごはんに (hirugohan ni) means 'at lunch'.

questions.question_text:
Fill in the particle.
```text
えきは ここ ____ ちかいです。 (eki wa koko ____ chikai desu.)  # The station is close from here.
```

options.A: を (o)
options.B: で (de)
options.C: と (to)
options.D: から (kara)

questions.explanation: から (kara) marks the starting point ('from'): ここから ちかいです (koko kara chikai desu). Its counterpart まで (made) marks the endpoint. を (o), で (de) and と (to) cannot express the 'from here' relation with ちかい (chikai, close). Another example: くうこうは ここから とおいです (kūkō wa koko kara tōi desu), 'The airport is far from here'.

questions.question_text: Build the description with $\text{person} + \text{wa} + \text{part} + \text{ga} + (\text{adj}_1 - \text{i} + \text{kute}) + \text{adj}_2 + \text{desu}$. Which sentence says 'His hair is black and short' (くろい kuroi = black, みじかい mijikai = short, かみ kami = hair)?

options.A: かれは かみが くろくて みじかいです (kare wa kami ga kurokute mijikai desu)
options.B: かれは かみが くろいくて みじかいです (kare wa kami ga kuroikute mijikai desu)
options.C: かれは かみが くろで みじかいです (kare wa kami ga kuro de mijikai desu)
options.D: かれは かみを くろくて みじかいです (kare wa kami o kurokute mijikai desu)

questions.explanation: The first adjective takes the connective form (くろい kuroi → くろくて kurokute) and the last one stays in its plain form before です (desu). The feature (かみ kami) is marked with が (ga) under the topic かれは (kare wa). を (o) would mark an object of an action verb, and keeping the い (i) before くて (kute) is wrong. Another example: かのじょは かみが ながくて くろいです (kanojo wa kami ga nagakute kuroi desu).

questions.question_text: Sequences of nouns and adjectives follow $N_1 + \text{de}, \ N_2 + \text{de}, \ \text{adj} + \text{desu}$. Which sentence says 'Maria is Brazilian, a teacher, and kind'?

options.A: マリアさんは ブラジルじんくて、せんせいくて、やさしいです (Maria-san wa burajirujinkute, senseikute, yasashii desu)
options.B: マリアさんは ブラジルじんで、せんせいで、やさしいです (Maria-san wa burajirujin de, sensei de, yasashii desu)
options.C: マリアさんは ブラジルじんの、せんせいの、やさしいです (Maria-san wa burajirujin no, sensei no, yasashii desu)
options.D: マリアさんは ブラジルじんな、せんせいな、やさしいです (Maria-san wa burajirujin na, sensei na, yasashii desu)

questions.explanation: Each noun in a chain takes で (de) as the link, and only the final item carries です (desu): ブラジルじんで (burajirujin de), せんせいで (sensei de), やさしいです (yasashii desu). くて (kute) is reserved for i-adjectives, の (no) joins nouns inside a noun phrase and な (na) goes only before a noun. Another example: いしゃで、いそがしいです (isha de, isogashii desu).

questions.question_text: Wishes follow $\text{verb}_{masu} - \text{masu} + \text{tai desu}$. The polite form of 'come' is きます (kimasu). Which sentence says 'I want to come to the hotel'?

options.A: ホテルへ くたいです (hoteru e kutai desu)
options.B: ホテルへ きますたいです (hoteru e kimasu tai desu)
options.C: ホテルへ きたいです (hoteru e kitai desu)
options.D: ホテルへ きいたいです (hoteru e kiitai desu)

questions.explanation: Remove ます (masu) from きます (kimasu) to get the stem き (ki), then add たいです (tai desu): きたいです (kitai desu). The dictionary form くる (kuru) would give くたい (kutai), which is wrong because the rule starts from the ます (masu) form. Another example: すしを たべたいです (sushi o tabetai desu), 'I want to eat sushi'.

questions.question_text: Ages are built as $\text{tens} + \text{units} + \text{sai}$ (tens first). Which form means '35 years old'? (さん san = 3, じゅう jū = 10, ご go = 5)

options.A: ごじゅうさんさい (gojūsansai)
options.B: さんごじゅうさい (sangojūsai)
options.C: さんじゅうさんさい (sanjūsansai)
options.D: さんじゅうごさい (sanjūgosai)

questions.explanation: Japanese numbers are read like the arithmetic: 3 tens + 5 = さん＋じゅう＋ご (san + jū + go), then the age counter さい (sai): さんじゅうごさい (sanjūgosai). ごじゅうさんさい (gojūsansai) is 53 and さんじゅうさんさい (sanjūsansai) is 33. An exception is 20 = はたち (hatachi).

questions.question_text: Prices are built as $\text{hundreds} + \text{tens} + \text{en}$. Which expression gives 350 yen (300 + 50), keeping in mind the sound change of 300 (さん san + ひゃく hyaku)?

options.A: さんびゃくごじゅうえん (sanbyaku gojū en)
options.B: さんひゃくごじゅうえん (sanhyaku gojū en)
options.C: さんびゃくじゅうごえん (sanbyaku jūgo en)
options.D: ごじゅうさんびゃくえん (gojū sanbyaku en)

questions.explanation: Numbers are read from the largest unit down: 300 = さんびゃく (sanbyaku, with the voiced びゃく byaku) and 50 = ごじゅう (gojū), then えん (en). さんびゃくじゅうごえん (sanbyaku jūgo en) is 315 and ごじゅうさんびゃくえん (gojū sanbyaku en) is nonsensical ordering. Another example: にひゃくごじゅうえん (nihyaku gojū en), 250 yen.

questions.question_text: Build the sentence with $\text{possessor} + \text{no} + \text{item} + \text{wa} + \text{place} + \text{desu}$. Which sentence says 'Mr. Tanaka's ticket is here'? (きっぷ kippu = ticket, ここ koko = here)

options.A: たなかさんは きっぷの ここです (Tanaka-san wa kippu no koko desu)
options.B: たなかさんの きっぷは ここです (Tanaka-san no kippu wa koko desu)
options.C: きっぷの たなかさんは ここです (kippu no Tanaka-san wa koko desu)
options.D: たなかさんの ここは きっぷです (Tanaka-san no koko wa kippu desu)

questions.explanation: The possessive の (no) attaches the owner to the item (たなかさんの きっぷ Tanaka-san no kippu), the whole phrase is the topic with は (wa), and the location word completes the sentence with です (desu). Swapping owner and item, or placing の (no) after the ticket, changes who owns what. Another example: ホテルの ちずは あそこです (hoteru no chizu wa asoko desu).

questions.question_text: Use $\text{ano} + N + \text{wa} + \text{na-adj} + \text{de}, \ \text{i-adj} + \text{desu}$. Which sentence says 'That restaurant over there is famous and expensive'? (ゆうめい yūmei = famous, a na-adjective; たかい takai = expensive)

options.A: あれ レストランは ゆうめいで、たかいです (are resutoran wa yūmei de, takai desu)
options.B: あの レストランは ゆうめいくて、たかいです (ano resutoran wa yūmeikute, takai desu)
options.C: あの レストランは ゆうめいで、たかいです (ano resutoran wa yūmei de, takai desu)
options.D: あの レストランは ゆうめいな、たかいです (ano resutoran wa yūmei na, takai desu)

questions.explanation: あの (ano) is the demonstrative that modifies a noun for things far from both speakers; あれ (are) is a pronoun and cannot sit before a noun. ゆうめい (yūmei) ends in い (i) but is a na-adjective, so it links with で (de), not くて (kute). Another example: この ホテルは きれいで、やすいです (kono hoteru wa kirei de, yasui desu).

questions.question_text: Combine two i-adjectives, the second one negative, with $\text{adj}_1 - \text{i} + \text{kute}, \ \text{adj}_2 - \text{i} + \text{kunai} + \text{desu}$. Which sentence says 'The room is big and not expensive'?

options.A: へやは おおきいで、たかくないです (heya wa ōkii de, takakunai desu)
options.B: へやは おおきくて、たかいじゃ ありません (heya wa ōkikute, takai ja arimasen)
options.C: へやは おおきくて、たかくありませんです (heya wa ōkikute, takaku arimasen desu)
options.D: へやは おおきくて、たかくないです (heya wa ōkikute, takakunai desu)

questions.explanation: Both adjectives are i-adjectives, so the first becomes おおきくて (ōkikute) and the second takes the negative たかくない (takakunai) plus です (desu). で (de) does not follow an i-adjective directly, and じゃ ありません (ja arimasen) is the noun/na-adjective pattern. Another example: かばんは かるくて、やすいです (kaban wa karukute, yasui desu), 'The bag is light and cheap'.

questions.question_text: The particle も (mo, 'also') takes the place of は (wa), が (ga) or を (o), following $N + \text{o} \to N + \text{mo}$. Which sentence correctly says 'Water too, please'? (みず mizu = water, ください kudasai = please give)

options.A: みずも ください (mizu mo kudasai)
options.B: みずを も ください (mizu o mo kudasai)
options.C: みずも を ください (mizu mo o kudasai)
options.D: みずが も ください (mizu ga mo kudasai)

questions.explanation: も (mo) replaces は (wa), が (ga) or を (o) rather than stacking after it: みずを ください (mizu o kudasai) becomes みずも ください (mizu mo kudasai). Another example: わたしは コーヒーを のみます (watashi wa kōhī o nomimasu) → わたしも コーヒーを のみます (watashi mo kōhī o nomimasu), 'I also drink coffee'.

questions.question_text: Sentences are built as $\text{time} + \text{ni} + \text{place} + \text{de} + \text{object} + \text{o} + \text{verb}$ with the verb last. Which sentence says 'At lunch I eat bread at the restaurant' (ひるごはん hirugohan = lunch, レストラン resutoran = restaurant)?

options.A: たべます ひるごはんに レストランで パンを (tabemasu hirugohan ni resutoran de pan o)
options.B: ひるごはんに レストランで パンを たべます (hirugohan ni resutoran de pan o tabemasu)
options.C: ひるごはんに レストランを パンで たべます (hirugohan ni resutoran o pan de tabemasu)
options.D: ひるごはんで レストランに パンが たべます (hirugohan de resutoran ni pan ga tabemasu)

questions.explanation: Japanese verbs come last, with each phrase tagged by its particle: に (ni) for time, で (de) for the place of an action, を (o) for the object. Swapping the particles changes the roles, and putting the verb first breaks the order. Another example: ばんごはんに うちで カレーを たべます (bangohan ni uchi de karē o tabemasu), 'At dinner I eat curry at home'.

questions.question_text: Requests follow $\text{verb}_{te} + \text{kudasai}$. For verbs ending in う (u), such as かいます (kaimasu) → かう (kau), the て-form (te-form) ends in って (tte). Which sentence says 'Please buy a ticket'?

options.A: きっぷを かいて ください (kippu o kaite kudasai)
options.B: きっぷを かいで ください (kippu o kaide kudasai)
options.C: きっぷを かって ください (kippu o katte kudasai)
options.D: きっぷを かりて ください (kippu o karite kudasai)

questions.explanation: かう (kau, 'buy') ends in う (u), so its て-form (te-form) is かって (katte): かって ください (katte kudasai). かいて (kaite) comes from かく (kaku, 'write'), かいで (kaide) from a verb ending in ぐ (gu), and かりて (karite) from かりる (kariru, 'borrow'). Another example: ちずを かって ください (chizu o katte kudasai).

questions.question_text: Compare 「レストランで たべます」 (resutoran de tabemasu, 'I eat at the restaurant') with 「ここに あります」 (koko ni arimasu, 'It is here'). Why does the place take で (de) in one and に (ni) in the other?

options.A: で (de) is for indoor places and に (ni) for outdoor places
options.B: で (de) is for plural nouns and に (ni) for singular nouns
options.C: Both are interchangeable; only politeness differs
options.D: で (de) marks where an action takes place, while に (ni) marks where something exists with あります (arimasu)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: で (de) for the place of an action versus に (ni) for location of existence. With action verbs like たべます (tabemasu), the setting takes で (de). With existence verbs like あります (arimasu), the location takes に (ni): ホテルは えきの ちかくに あります (hoteru wa eki no chikaku ni arimasu). Another example: こうえんで あるきます (kōen de arukimasu), 'I walk in the park'.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says 'I eat bread and eggs'?

options.A: パンと たまごを たべます (pan to tamago o tabemasu)
options.B: パンの たまごを たべます (pan no tamago o tabemasu)
options.C: パンが たまごを たべます (pan ga tamago o tabemasu)
options.D: パンに たまごを たべます (pan ni tamago o tabemasu)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: と (to) joining nouns as 'and'. と (to) connects the items of a list and the final noun takes the particle: パンと たまごを (pan to tamago o). の (no) would make 'egg of bread', and が (ga) turns bread into the eater. Another example: あかい くつと しろい くつ (akai kutsu to shiroi kutsu), 'red shoes and white shoes'.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says 'I want a map'?

options.A: ちずを ほしいです (chizu o hoshii desu)
options.B: ちずが ほしいです (chizu ga hoshii desu)
options.C: ちずに ほしいです (chizu ni hoshii desu)
options.D: ちずが ほしたいです (chizu ga hoshitai desu)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: が (ga) with ほしい (hoshii, 'want [a thing]'). ほしい (hoshii) is an i-adjective of desire, so the wanted object takes が (ga). It is not formed with たい (tai), which attaches to verb stems. Another example: おみやげが ほしいです (omiyage ga hoshii desu), 'I want a souvenir'.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says 'The bag is good and cheap' (いい ii = good, やすい yasui = cheap)?

options.A: かばんは いくて、やすいです (kaban wa ikute, yasui desu)
options.B: かばんは いいくて、やすいです (kaban wa iikute, yasui desu)
options.C: かばんは よくて、やすいです (kaban wa yokute, yasui desu)
options.D: かばんは いいで、やすいです (kaban wa ii de, yasui desu)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: irregular connective form いい (ii) → よくて (yokute). いい (ii) is a variant of よい (yoi), and the connective form is built on よ (yo). The same stem gives よくない (yokunai, 'not good'). Another example: ほんは よくて、おもしろいです (hon wa yokute, omoshiroi desu).

questions.question_text:
Which word completes 'Is that hat over there yours?'

`____ ぼうしは あなたのですか。 (____ bōshi wa anata no desu ka.)`

options.A: あれ (are)
options.B: あそこ (asoko)
options.C: ああ (aa)
options.D: あの (ano)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: demonstrative modifier あの (ano) before a noun. あの (ano) 'that over there' must be followed by a noun (あの ぼうし ano bōshi). あれ (are) is a pronoun that stands for the whole thing (あれは あなたのぼうしですか are wa anata no bōshi desu ka), and あそこ (asoko) is a place word. Another example: その くつは たかいです (sono kutsu wa takai desu).

questions.question_text:
Which word completes 'Which person is Maria?'

`マリアさんは ____ ひとですか。 (Maria-san wa ____ hito desu ka.)`

options.A: どの (dono)
options.B: どれ (dore)
options.C: どこ (doko)
options.D: どんな (donna)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: question modifier どの (dono, 'which') before a noun, parallel to この／その／あの (kono / sono / ano). どれ (dore) stands alone as a pronoun ('which one'), どこ (doko) means 'where', and どんな (donna) asks 'what kind of'. Another example: どの バスが えきへ いきますか (dono basu ga eki e ikimasu ka), 'Which bus goes to the station?'

questions.question_text: Which question correctly asks a teacher's age?

options.A: せんせいは なんにんですか (sensei wa nannin desu ka)
options.B: せんせいは なんさいですか (sensei wa nansai desu ka)
options.C: せんせいは いくらですか (sensei wa ikura desu ka)
options.D: せんせいは なんじですか (sensei wa nanji desu ka)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: the age counter さい (sai) with なん (nan, 'how many'): なんさい (nansai). Each counter pairs with its own noun: なんにん (nannin) counts people, いくら (ikura) is a price, なんじ (nanji) is the time. For a polite version use おいくつですか (oikutsu desu ka). Another example: ともだちは なんさいですか (tomodachi wa nansai desu ka).

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly orders 'two apples, please'?

options.A: りんごを にさい ください (ringo o nisai kudasai)
options.B: りんごを ふたり ください (ringo o futari kudasai)
options.C: りんごを ふたつ ください (ringo o futatsu kudasai)
options.D: りんごを ふたつを ください (ringo o futatsu o kudasai)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: the native counting series ひとつ (hitotsu), ふたつ (futatsu), みっつ (mittsu)… for general objects, placed after the noun and its particle. さい (sai) is for age and ふたり (futari) for two people. The number word is not followed by another を (o). Another example: みずを ひとつ ください (mizu o hitotsu kudasai), 'One water, please'.

questions.question_text: Which form is the formal negative of 'It is expensive' (たかいです takai desu)?

options.A: たかいありません (takai arimasen)
options.B: たかくじゃ ありません (takaku ja arimasen)
options.C: たかくでは ありません (takaku de wa arimasen)
options.D: たかくありません (takaku arimasen)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: formal negative of i-adjectives with くありません (ku arimasen). Replace the final い (i) with く (ku) and add ありません (arimasen): たかくありません (takaku arimasen). The variant たかくないです (takakunai desu) is equally common. じゃ ありません (ja arimasen) and では ありません (de wa arimasen) attach directly to nouns and na-adjectives, not to く (ku) forms.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly says 'My friend is at the station'?

options.A: ともだちは えきに います (tomodachi wa eki ni imasu)
options.B: ともだちは えきに あります (tomodachi wa eki ni arimasu)
options.C: ともだちは えきに いきます (tomodachi wa eki ni ikimasu)
options.D: ともだちは えきに ください (tomodachi wa eki ni kudasai)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: います (imasu) for the existence of people and animals versus あります (arimasu) for things. ともだち (tomodachi) is a living being, so the verb is います (imasu); a map would be ちずが あります (chizu ga arimasu). いきます (ikimasu) means 'go', which changes the meaning. Another example: ねこは へやに います (neko wa heya ni imasu), 'The cat is in the room'.

questions.question_text: Which question correctly asks 'Is that a quiet town?' (しずか shizuka = quiet, まち machi = town)?

options.A: それは しずかい まちですか (sore wa shizukai machi desu ka)
options.B: それは しずかな まちですか (sore wa shizuka na machi desu ka)
options.C: それは しずか まちですか (sore wa shizuka machi desu ka)
options.D: それは しずかで まちですか (sore wa shizuka de machi desu ka)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: na-adjective + な (na) + noun, with か (ka) turning the statement into a question. しずか (shizuka) is a na-adjective, so しずかな まち (shizuka na machi). Using い (i), dropping the particle, or using で (de) before a noun are all errors. Another example: きれいな へやですか (kirei na heya desu ka), 'Is it a clean room?'

questions.question_text: Which question correctly asks 'What did you eat?'

options.A: なにを たべますでしたか (nani o tabemasu deshita ka)
options.B: なにを たべたますか (nani o tabetamasu ka)
options.C: なにを たべましたか (nani o tabemashita ka)
options.D: なにが たべましたか (nani ga tabemashita ka)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: polite past ～ました (~mashita) with か (ka) for a question. The object question word takes を (o): なにを (nani o). たべました (tabemashita) is the past of たべます (tabemasu); *たべますでした* (tabemasu deshita) mixes two forms. Another example: なにを のみましたか (nani o nomimashita ka), 'What did you drink?'

questions.question_text: A asks `これは あなたの かばんですか` (kore wa anata no kaban desu ka, 'Is this your bag?'). The bag belongs to a friend. Which reply is correct?

options.A: はい、ともだちの かばんです (hai, tomodachi no kaban desu)
options.B: いいえ、わたしの かばんです (iie, watashi no kaban desu)
options.C: はい、わたしの かばんじゃ ありません (hai, watashi no kaban ja arimasen)
options.D: いいえ、ともだちの かばんです (iie, tomodachi no kaban desu)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: answering a yes/no question with correction. When the answer is 'no', start with いいえ (iie) and give the correct information with です (desu) rather than repeating the denial. はい (hai) would confirm that it is your bag, and いいえ、わたしの かばんです (iie, watashi no kaban desu) would contradict itself. Another example: いいえ、カナダじんです (iie, kanadajin desu), 'No, (I am) Canadian'.

questions.question_text:
Which word fits the gap to give 'He is quiet. But he is funny.'?

`かれは しずかです。____、おもしろいです。 (kare wa shizuka desu. ____, omoshiroi desu.)`

options.A: でも (demo)
options.B: そして (soshite)
options.C: じゃあ (jā)
options.D: たぶん (tabun)

questions.explanation: Grammar point: sentence-initial でも (demo, 'but') for contrast versus そして (soshite, 'and then/and'), which adds information. じゃあ (jā) means 'then/well' and たぶん (tabun) means 'probably'. The same contrast can be built inside one sentence with が (ga): しずかですが、おもしろいです (shizuka desu ga, omoshiroi desu).
